161	## 9. Caveats
162	
163	Host recomputes extents/joins/file and package path totality from membership+snapshot. Host does **not** recompute native symbol rows or the true examined set. `programEntry` is not a complete program key (Rust cfg/features live in universe H). Checker receipt is not full graph replay. GR6 hashing, G3–G9, GR8 majors remain open.
164

250	  bundles grammars for `rust`, `typescript`, `javascript`, `json`, `toml`,
251	  `markdown` and `yaml`; the shared discovery rule routes all fourteen of their
252	  suffixes to membership `syntax-only`, reason `grammar-only`. An earlier
253	  revision of this section let the grammar descriptor name only the three code
254	  languages and asserted equality with the `body-language-version` `languageId`
255	  enum as a drift check. That check proved the enum matched itself: it could not
256	  express the four data/document grammars the host has always shipped, so the
257	  promise directly above — *any* file whose extension maps to a bundled grammar —
258	  was unrepresentable for them. The descriptor now covers exactly the bundled
259	  set, and each row declares its **`syntaxClass`**.
260	
261	**`code` versus `data-document`: the distinction the contracts already draw.**
262	This is not a new narrowing; it is an existing law made machine-readable.
263	
264	- **`code`** — `rust`, `typescript`, `javascript`. §6.3 defines body spans as
265	  function, method, closure/lambda, `impl` item and block bodies, publishes the
266	  L2/L3 normalisation tables for exactly these languages, and puts
267	  `languageId ∈ {typescript, javascript, rust}` in the clone preimage. These
268	  grammars bear clone body identity and the code-construct syntax relations, and
269	  their `languageId` **must** be a member of the `body-language-version` enum.
270	- **`data-document`** — `json`, `toml`, `markdown`, `yaml`. These formats have no
271	  such body spans, and this kit publishes **no** tokenisation, `literalKind`
272	  mapping or normalisation law for them anywhere. Their files are grammar-only
273	  members — accounted, inventoried, and never `unsupported-file` — bearing
274	  `file`/`package`/`vcs-change` inventory evidence under the syntax universe.
275	  They mint **no** body identity, no suffix of theirs appears in the grammar
276	  dialect table, and their `languageId` **must not** be in the
277	  `body-language-version` enum, since it could never appear in a clone preimage.
278	
279	Both directions are enforced at grammar-bundle admission: a data grammar
280	claiming `code`, a code grammar demoted to `data-document`, and a row claiming a
281	suffix the discovery table routes to another language each refuse with their own
282	typed cause. What is held equal to the `body-language-version` enum is therefore
283	the **`code` subset**, not the whole bundle — which accounts for all seven
284	languages instead of ignoring four.
285	
286	Claiming `declares`/`literal`/`control-flow` facts for a data format would
287	require a tokenisation law this kit does not publish, and inventing one would be
288	precisely the fabricated-semantics failure the syntax-only universe exists to
289	prevent. If the product later wants data-format syntax facts, it needs a
290	published tokenisation and `literalKind` law first; that is a bounded future
291	capability and this matrix does not promise it today.
292	
293	An unbundled language stays unrepresentable: `.py` has no bundled grammar, is
294	not in the descriptor vocabulary, and its files remain `unsupported-file` with
295	reason `no-bundled-grammar`.
296	
297	**The capability law binds facts and Coverage, not just descriptors.** Validating
298	a grammar bundle's declared `syntaxClass` constrains what a bundle may say about
299	itself; it does not constrain what a Run may claim. An earlier revision enforced
300	the registry only there, and full Runs consequently admitted a Markdown-anchored
301	`declares` fact, a **complete** empty `declares`/`clones` Coverage over a
302	data-only repository, and `references@resolved-binding` under a universe whose
303	own record declares `resolutionAttempted: false`. The registry is therefore
304	consulted at the two boundaries that decide what a Run asserts, and at neither
305	does it consult the claimed coverage value, the caller-declared class, or
306	whether facts happen to exist:
307	
308	- **Every admitted fact.** A `fact2` under a syntax universe is admissible only
309	  if **every one of its anchor paths** is read by a **selected** grammar whose
310	  registry capability set contains that `relation@rung`. The anchor is the file
311	  the body was actually read from, so a Markdown-anchored code fact refuses in a
312	  mixed repository exactly as it does in a data-only one
313	  (`SYNTAX_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED_FACT`). **Inventory capabilities are exempt
314	  here as well as at the scope boundary below** — the exemption belongs to the
315	  *relation*, not to the boundary. An earlier revision wrote this bullet as an
316	  unconditional every-anchor rule and stated the exemption only in the scope
317	  bullet, so the two bullets contradicted each other: a literal implementer
318	  refused a `file@enumerated` fact for `tool/main.py` while the scope bullet had
319	  just promised that the same path's inventory Coverage was unconditionally
320	  `complete` — an inventoried file that is authoritatively absent. An inventory
321	  fact is not read by a grammar at all; it *is* the inventory row, the manifest
322	  declaration or the VCS observation, so there is no grammar for it to be gated
323	  on. (The relation registry's `anchorLaw` independently gives the inventory
324	  class **zero** anchors, so such a fact names no anchor path for this bullet to
325	  test either; the two laws agree and neither leans on the other.) The exemption
326	  is from grammar ownership **only**: the relation's snapshot joins, own-scope
327	  attribution and the anchor law all still bind, and no code fact becomes
328	  admissible because some other anchor in the Run sits on a supported path.
329	- **Every requested scope, including an empty view.** A `subject-scope` under a
330	  syntax universe is judged on its committed **examined extent** — the source
331	  inventory of the snapshot it names. **Inventory** capabilities
332	  (`file@enumerated`, `package@manifest-declared`, `vcs-change@vcs-reported`) are
333	  **always** available and are deliberately **not** grammar-gated: a snapshot
334	  inventories every file it contains, including ones no bundled grammar reads,
335	  and requiring a grammar per inventory row would silently narrow that promise.
336	  A **code** capability requires at least one path in that extent to be read by a
337	  selected `code` grammar. A capability no selected grammar bears is unavailable —
338	  which is every semantic rung and `unresolved-edge` under a syntax universe,
339	  exactly as the matrix already says.
340	
341	**A promised inventory capability represents every inventoried path, and a
342	`complete` inventory result may not hide an omitted one.** These are two halves
343	of one promise and the second was missing. `file@enumerated` is **total** over
344	the snapshot inventory: a snapshot inventories exactly the files it contains, so
345	every inventoried path has exactly one `file` fact, and over a **complete**
346	`file@enumerated` Coverage the predicate `exists file where path=P` is
347	authoritative. A complete result that retains no fact for an inventoried subject
348	therefore asserts that an inventoried file is absent, and that graph closed —
349	nothing derived the obligation, so nothing compared it. A `complete`
350	`file@enumerated` Coverage must now carry an admitted `file@enumerated` fact for
351	every one of its subjects that the snapshot inventory contains
352	(`COVERAGE_INVENTORY_TOTALITY_OMITS_PATH`), derived at Run closure from the
353	retained view's own facts and the retained inventory.
354	
355	**A fact discharges the obligation of the scope it actually belongs to.** The
356	match is on every coordinate the registry's `matchOn` lists — the four
357	`CoverageKeyV2` coordinates other than the commitment itself
358	(`relation`, `resolution`, `sourceUniverse`, `targetUniverse`) plus the owning
359	`snapshotId`. Matching relation and rung *alone* is not enough in a view carrying
360	more than one universe, and this is not hypothetical: the view-level fact/scope
361	join is **existential** — each fact need only agree with *some* scope on relation,
362	rung and both universes — so a TypeScript `file` fact is lawfully present in a
363	view that also carries a syntax-universe `file@enumerated` scope, and while the
364	match was two-coordinate it *paid that scope's missing-file obligation*. A
365	complete Run exhibited exactly that: two `complete` scopes over `a.ts`, only the
366	TypeScript fact, admitted. Totality is a claim about what **this** universe
367	examined, so it must be discharged by evidence produced in this universe; a fact
368	from another universe is a different interpretation of the same bytes, not the
369	same observation. The two-universe Run in which *each* scope carries its own fact
370	remains lawful and is retained as a positive control. `snapshotId` is listed
371	although Run closure already forces it on every fact and scope: this law reads one
372	scope's obligation out of a *shared* view, and a join that silently leans on an
373	invariant enforced elsewhere is the same implicit coupling that produced the
374	cross-universe defect.
375	
376	Two things the law deliberately does not require: a subject the snapshot does
377	**not** contain is owed nothing —
378	the host examined the question and the file is genuinely absent, which is the
379	one case a universal negative over inventory exists to serve — and an `unknown`
380	result carrying its disclosed deficiency is owed nothing, which keeps a
381	partially examined inventory representable rather than forcing a false
382	`complete`. `package@manifest-declared` and `vcs-change@vcs-reported` are **not**
383	total and owe nothing: most paths declare no package and most were not changed,
384	so their empty results are ordinary findings. Which relations owe totality is
385	stated in the relation registry (`coverageTotality`), where only `file` has a
386	row, and never inferred. This is the specific rule that identity §3's "partition
387	the claimed universe without overlaps or omissions" defers to: the **disjointness**
388	half is general, applies within the full owning
389	`(snapshotId, relation, resolution, sourceUniverse, targetUniverse)` tuple, and is
390	decided at retained Run closure against the registry's own
391	`coveragePartitionLaw`; the **omission** half is discharged only where this
392	registry carries a `coverageTotality` row. For the nine `symbol`-kind relations it
393	carries none, and the reason is the trust boundary stated below — symbol-to-file
394	attribution is not re-derivable from the retained Run — so no fact-per-symbol
395	obligation exists there. Evaluator3 separately requires the selected symbol
396	inventory and accounts for required work over its independently retained census
397	(identity §4). A symbol may have no call/reference fact, while a whole expected
398	inventory or work partition cannot silently disappear. Disjointness still applies, because it
399	asks a different question: not what was examined, but whether one interpretation
400	claimed a subject twice.
401	
402	**How many spans a fact cites is a registry law, not an implementer's choice.**
403	`fact.anchors` carried no `minItems`, and only `clones` ever stated a
404	cardinality, so every published predicate over the array — the `file` row's
405	`anchorPathField`, and the every-anchor rule above — was universally quantified
406	and therefore *vacuously true* at zero anchors. It neither permitted nor forbade
407	the unanchored spelling, and both spellings of one `file@enumerated` claim closed
408	a Run with different `fact2` identities. The relation registry now carries a
409	closed `anchorLaw` on every relation, in three classes: `source-text` (the nine
410	code relations) needs **at least one** span, because a code fact is read from
411	source text and an unanchored one names no file that could have been read;
412	`body-identity` (`clones`) is **exactly one**, unchanged; and `inventory`
413	(`file`, `package`, `vcs-change`) is **exactly zero**, because such a fact's
414	whole semantic input is its payload, which the relation's own snapshot joins
415	already bind. Zero is also the only cardinality *every* inventoried path can
416	satisfy — including a `vcs-change` whose `changeKind` is `deleted`, whose path is
417	by construction not in the snapshot and can carry no anchor at all. The
418	`source-text` class deliberately imposes **no additional relation-specific
419	maximum** and no canonical extent *beyond the common schema bounds* —
420	`fact.anchors` already carries `maxItems: 100000` and `uniqueItems`, and those
421	continue to apply to every relation; what the class declines is a per-relation
422	ceiling or a canonical span set, not the shared one. Which spans a producer cites
423	is a real statement about what it read, so two producers citing different spans
424	have produced different semantic descriptors and legitimately mint different
425	identities. Nothing here promises cross-provider anchor identity for code facts. Two things this also closes that the previous
426	wording did not: an unanchored *code* fact was refused only inside this
427	syntax-universe guard and closed a Run under a TypeScript or Rust universe, and
428	`anchorPathField` existed only on the `file` row, so a `package` fact anchored
429	into an unrelated file closed a Run. One law now covers every relation in every
430	universe (`FACT_ANCHOR_CARDINALITY`).
431	
432	An **unselected** grammar lends no capability: selection is committed in the
433	universe identity, so a bundle that ships a Rust grammar the universe did not
434	select cannot make `declares@syntactic` available for `.rs` files.
435	
436	**An unavailable request is disclosed, not answered, and never refused outright.**
437	The capability is retained and representable: the scope closes a Run and carries
438	`coverage: unknown` with `deficiency: language-tier-unsupported` and
439	`nativeCause: capability-missing` — both already in the existing vocabulary, and
440	mapped in §10. A **false `complete`** for an unavailable capability, a wrong or
441	null cause, and a wrong deficiency each refuse with their own reason
442	(`SYNTAX_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED_SCOPE`, `…_CAUSE_MISMATCH`,
443	`…_DEFICIENCY_MISMATCH`). No syntax Run is made blanket-indeterminate to achieve
444	this: a data-grammar inventory Run and a code-grammar `declares`/`clones` Run
445	both still close with a genuine `complete` and no deficiency.
446	
447	This particular guard — the one decided by the **selected grammar rows** — is
448	**syntax-universe specific**. Every *semantic* capability of the TypeScript and
449	Rust universes is unchanged, including all five semantic relations, and the Rust
450	compilation-ownership guards are untouched — see the ownership disclosure law in
451	§10, whose prerequisite is now derived from the actual universe kind so that a
452	grammar-only clone scope, which has no compilation unit at all, owes no
453	compiler-ownership obligation.
454	
455	It is **not** the only scope-capability guard, and an earlier revision of this
456	paragraph read as if it were. A separate and weaker law, stated in §10 and
457	published as
458	`identity-schemas.v3.json#/x-opensip-digest-domains/scopeCapabilityLaw`, applies
459	to **any** universe whose dialect form is a closed suffix table — TypeScript and
460	the syntax universe both — and asks only whether a scoped path's own suffix
461	selects a variant in the table that universe published. For the syntax universe
462	that condition is strictly weaker than the grammar law above and is implied by
463	it, because the capability registry's `data-document` class law already states
464	that **no suffix of a data grammar appears in the syntax dialect table**. For
465	TypeScript it is the *only* such law, and it is what a `clones` scope over
466	`package.json` is now answered by. Which guard reaches a given scope first,
467	however, is decided by what each boundary can see, not by which law is stronger.
468	The suffix law needs nothing but the scope's own paths, so the native Coverage
469	producer boundary already applies it to the one case it can judge from a single
470	record — a `source-path` relation carrying a body-identity join, which is
471	`clones` — whenever the caller hands it the owning universe's dialect, as Run
472	closure does. Closure runs that producer admission **before** any of its own
473	prerequisites, so a false claim of complete Coverage for a `clones` scope over
474	a path no dialect table lists is refused there, as a producer-admission failure
475	naming the source variant, before the grammar guard. The grammar law is neither weakened nor reordered: among
476	closure's own prerequisites it is still applied ahead of the suffix backstop,
477	and it remains the sole owner, under its own refusal names, of everything a
478	suffix table cannot see — the `symbol` relations, the other syntax relations,
479	and the selection case where a path's suffix *is* in the table but no selected

1	# Complete evaluator composition — contract v3
2	
3	This appendix is incorporated by product identity-and-evidence §4. Acceptance and implementation readiness are recorded separately. The scope here is the closed declarative policy evaluator; native extraction and candidate-only clone producers retain their own contracts. Enumeration and atom appendices provide the input population and exact atom laws. Their retained inputs are inputs to this composition, never expected output supplied by a provider.
4	
5	## 1. Explicit version dispatch and input binding
6	
7	`identity-schemas.v3.json` owns the new evaluator output profile. Changed H domains are finding3, proof3, evidence3, seal3, run3 and policy-derivation3. New subject3 identifies `{schemaVersion:3, universe, kind, nativeSubjectId}`, with packageManifestPath REQUIRED additionally for kind=package and forbidden otherwise. Native package names can repeat across first-party manifests in one universe; this path distinguishes their evaluation coordinates without inventing a native ID. Package fact source binding compares both packageName and manifestPath. Incoming package attribution must distinguish the manifest or remain unknown; a name alone cannot select among duplicate packages. Native H identities, snapshot2, closure2, import2, plan2, scope2, fact2, coverage2, view2, exec-plan2 and finding-key2 retain their recipes and record shapes. A changed parameter/schema value changes ancestor identity normally; unchanged record shape does not require relabelling its domain. Explicit version dispatch must reject mixed output-major graphs. Never stamp historical outputs with new prefixes or accept them as new proofs.
8	
9	Exactly one EnumerationPlanV1 and one EvaluatorEmissionPlanV1 parameter are required for this evaluator. `analysis-spec.parameters` names exact document bytes and C(payload) bytes. Neither parameter contains PlanId or analysisSpecDigest. The emission parameter names the independent resolved policy digest and one binding for EVERY policy rule. `ruleId`, contributionId, ruleStableId and semanticsMajor equal policy. Its detectorClosure is a selected closure of kind detector. A provider or evaluator closure cannot stand in for it. The evaluator does not infer an undocumented closure-to-contribution manifest lookup: the explicit binding is part of the committed Plan. Changing it changes Plan.
10	
11	Emission profile declarative-subject-v1 uses path-stable logical correspondence. Other detector families may introduce their own reviewed emission profiles; they may not masquerade as this profile. PolicyDocumentV2 (schemaMajor2) and RuleProgramV2 (schemaVersion2) add the atom endpoint and typed test filters. WaiverSetV1 and ScopeDocumentV1 retain their original owner document and bytes. Predicate-witness is canonical-record schemaVersion3, without an H prefix. Program predicate addresses retain their existing closed grammar and exact policy digest joins. The fingerprint namespace `(ruleStableId,semanticsMajor)` must be unique across all emission rows, including disabled rules. Per-row requiredForEvaluatorMajors=[3] enforces the two required parameters; the generic class zeroIsLegal law remains for other consumers.
12	
13	The proof requires `executionInputsDigest`, the raw SHA-256 of the exact retained
14	`ExecutionInputsV1` canonical record. `evaluationInputRefs` equals its selected
15	references plus that one manifest reference. Reconstruction re-admits stage
16	receipts, expected inventories, native work accounts, candidate returns and
17	selected imports before composing outputs. Required execution deficiencies
18	retain original typed causes and input references, including when policy rules
19	are disabled. Physical store inventories and operational retention receipts are
20	excluded from this semantic record and from Run identity.
21	
22	## 2. Independent population and enumeration
23	
24	Build the expected inventory locator set from the committed enumeration parameter, before inspecting any fact, Coverage, finding or witness. Require every listed outcome exactly once, including unavailable and complete-empty outcomes. Admit their producer/Plan/context/universe/membership/extent joins using the enumeration appendix. A missing expected outcome is an incomplete retained graph, not an empty population.
25	
26	For an enabled rule, select every admitted program of the rule's portable universe domain and required primary subject kind (export means symbol plus exported status). The closed policy universe token map is typescript→native.semantic-universe.typescript.v2, rust→native.semantic-universe.rust.v2, syntax→native.semantic-universe.syntax.v2. Unknown tokens refuse admission; historical illustrative tokens such as typescript-v2 are not additional implicit aliases. With no covering program binding for a rule domain/kind, its enumeration is incomplete with no-covering-program, never inferred complete-empty. Default recommendation resolves applicability when constructing policy; it does not silently disable an already committed enabled rule. Apply include/exclude to logical path, never opaque native IDs. Include absent or [] means all paths; exclusion wins. If the existing ScopeDocumentV1 parameter is selected, intersect its include/exclude globs as well; this is distinct from foundation plan.scopeDigest. Missing ScopeDocumentV1 is legal for ordinary analysis; baseline/comparison preserve their explicit selection requirement. Complete-empty requires a covering available binding, a complete expected inventory, and selection of zero subjects. A missing expected inventory pointer is structural refusal, not a manufactured unavailable outcome. Union duplicates only for the SAME `(universe,kind,nativeSubjectId)` (plus package manifest path for packages) after exact attribution/projection agreement. Distinct universes never merge. Source language is row attribution and can differ from engine domain.
27	
28	For export selection, exported rows are selected; not-exported rows are excluded; unknown rows enter unresolvedSubjectIds without being evaluated as definitely exported. Partial/unavailable inventory belongs to incompleteInventoryRefs even if it has zero rows. Known rows of a partial inventory are still evaluated. Each rule retains selected, unresolved, relevant inventories and incomplete inventories as `rule-enumeration`. A disabled rule retains state disabled and empty arrays, emits no predicates/findings, and has outcome disabled. This does not delete independent required execution obligations.
29	
30	## 3. Exact traversal, bounds and proof
31	
32	Evaluate the entire predicate tree postorder for every selected subject, retaining every node; do not omit branches after a short-circuit value. Address node p and children by the existing program-predicate address law. Boolean witnesses have kind boolean, children exactly the grammar's immediate child addresses, and empty fact/import/Coverage match arrays. Atomic witnesses have kind native-atom or imported-atom, no children, countLimit only for count-at-most, and exact matching/uncertain evidence and deficiency sets from the atom appendix. All input references are direct retained roots or members of an evaluated view as the identity closure permits; witnesses cannot add roots.
33	
34	Truth is strong Kleene: not reverses true/false and preserves indeterminate; and is false if any child false, true iff all true, otherwise indeterminate; or is true if any child true, false iff all false, otherwise indeterminate. Atomic known matches are preserved despite unrelated incomplete coverage: exists with known match is true, none with known match is false, count-at-most with known distinct count greater than the bound is false. The remaining cases require the atom-specific completeness law. all-covered assesses the requested rung and applicable native/import coverage, not a generic resolved-only bit.
35	
36	Retain all deficiency provenance in witnesses even when a known value dominates it. Root-indeterminate gating relevance is computed separately: for an indeterminate and/or node only its indeterminate children contribute blocking causes; a determinate root has no truth-blocking cause. Enumeration and required execution deficiencies remain independent of truth. Optional imported evidence can leave a root indeterminate with disclosure but does not acquire gating authority solely because none or not was used.
37	
38	A deterministic full-scan budget preflight is a semantics-preserving bound. Let S be selected subjects over enabled rules, N(r) all tree nodes, A(r) atoms, F all distinct input facts, I all imported observation addresses (whole-test execution is one address), K all Coverage records, and E total inventory rows plus expected inventory locators. Charge E + sum over (r,s) of [N(r) + A(r)*(F+I+K)] work units. Use checked unsigned 64-bit arithmetic, no host timing; any intermediate overflow is budget-exceeded. Unresolved and unseen subjects are never evaluated later under this charge: known selected subjects are the entire actual evaluation set, and independent population uncertainty remains retained. No late population addition under the same proof is permitted. This upper bound is independent of findings, values and optimization. If greater than Plan budget, produce explicit budget-exhausted output before node evaluation: empty predicates/findings, actual enumeration records, per-enabled-rule indeterminate outcomes where gating, and an execution budget-exhausted deficiency. Known rule matches are not claimed when never evaluated. Disabled rule records remain disabled. Optimization may use fewer actual scans, but cannot change this reference admission/result. Array/C-byte output bounds are separately enforced; overflow refuses with EVALUATION.OUTPUT_BOUND_EXCEEDED / OUTPUT.SERIALIZATION_FAILED (operational-failed, faultCause=output-serialization), never truncation or a successful empty Run.
39	
40	## 4. Finding emission and correspondence
41	
42	For each subject with emitWhen=true emit exactly one full finding3 occurrence. Distinct selected universes keep distinct subject3 IDs and findings. messageCode is the rule's value if present, otherwise ruleId. The rule emission binding supplies detectorClosure; severity is the resolved rule severity. The finding's explicit ruleId disambiguates multiple policy rules sharing a detector contribution.
43	
44	The declarative-subject-v1 parameter record is `{schemaVersion:2,messageCode,parameters:{ruleId,subjectPath,qualifiedName,subjectKind,subjectLanguage,matchingFactCount,matchingImportCount}}`. Counts are distinct union of all descendant atom known matches, including branches whose truth did not control the root; counts never include uncertain matches. EvidenceRefs are exactly the root predicate-witness digest; every descendant known and uncertain fact; every descendant witness Coverage id (consulted, and allowed to be narrower than evaluationInputRefs); every descendant matching/uncertain observation importId; and every evaluationInputRefs member with domain=import (under whole-selection this equals the Plan import set). Observation addresses themselves remain on the witness. Enumeration and execution inventory refs remain on the proof. See §9.7. Full replay recomputes every value and citation. This fixed emission profile does not claim to reconstruct arbitrary third-party detector parameter templates.
45	
46	File/package discriminator is SHA256(C([])); their qualifiedName is admitted path/package name. Symbol uses this detectorClosure's nonempty ordered signatureTokens. Collision class is `(universe,subjectLanguage,kind,path,qualifiedName,detectorClosure)` across the independently enumerated population, not merely subjects which emitted. Identical projected signatures among distinct native IDs, empty/missing projection, anonymous unavailable name, or incomplete collision-class population cannot establish stable correspondence. Duplicate observations of the SAME subject3 are not a collision. Across distinct universes, independently equal logical descriptors may yield one stable fingerprint.
47	
48	Stable fingerprint descriptor remains finding-key2 with ruleStableId, detectorSemanticsMajor, subjectKey and empty relatedSubjectKeys for this unary declarative emission profile. Its key excludes universe. Related subjects are not invented from arbitrary predicate matches. Clone grouping/candidate producers retain their separate relation/projection contracts; no semantic similarity claim is introduced here.
49	
50	**Unmatched occurrences remain findings.** finding3 carries nullable fingerprint plus correspondence state matched|unmatched and a closed reason. Matched requires nonnull admitted finding-key2; unmatched requires null. Both retain subject3, ruleId, path/language/kind/name, parameters/severity/citations and can fail an ordinary current-Run gate. A missing stable key does not turn a known policy violation into pass. No encounter-order/body-hash surrogate is labelled stable. Unmatched correspondence is disclosed and cannot satisfy a fingerprint-target waiver; exact `(ruleId,subjectPath)` waiver may apply normally. Unknown export membership is not an unmatched occurrence because it was never definitely selected.
51	
52	## 5. Waiver and verdict composition
53	
54	Consume ONLY the effective WaiverSet bytes committed by Plan. Trust-clock expiry and duplicate target rejection were already resolved at Plan construction; replay does not read today's clock. An occurrence is waived iff any effective target equals its nonnull fingerprint or equals its exact `(ruleId,subjectPath)`. Preserve waived findings, list exact waivedFindingIds in proof, never remove their evidence. A waiver does not cure unknown subject population, unknown predicate truth, correspondence uncertainty needed by a comparison, or required execution failure.
55	
56	A rule gates iff enabled AND gate=true AND severity >= policy.gateSeverityAtLeast, with note<warning<error. A live unwaived finding for a gating rule makes its outcome fail. Otherwise a gating rule is indeterminate if its population is incomplete/unresolved or its root truth is indeterminate with at least one blocking native or required imported cause. Optional-only root unknown remains disclosed with rule outcome pass. An advisory rule's outcome is pass even if it retains findings/deficiencies. Required import obligations are assessed according to declared evidenceUse independently of a boolean branch suppressing their use; no undeclared import acquires authority. Disabled remains disabled.
57	
58	Required execution cells contribute independent executionDeficiencies even with all rules disabled or empty populations. Operational provider protocol violations remain invocation failure under the existing operational dominance law; they are not converted to semantic unknown. Among admitted semantic results, any gating rule fail wins; otherwise any gating rule indeterminate or required execution deficiency produces indeterminate; otherwise pass. Sealed verdict has only pass|fail|indeterminate. Surface advisory is a derived display for pass with live advisory findings. Each ruleResult includes all its emitted finding IDs and complete deficiencies, not just failing findings.
59	
60	## 6. Baseline, comparison, repair and surfaces
61	
62	For matched findings, group by fingerprint only AFTER byte-equal logical descriptor verification. Compute every BaselineEntry field from each occurrence's explicit rule/emission binding and waiver state. All fields, including optional legacyFingerprint presence/value, must agree. Legitimately different message/parameters/citations remain on the original findings and are not compared for baseline equality. Conflicting baseline projections refuse; no first/last writer wins. Comparison pivot presence is any admitted matched occurrence at that pivot, and waived presence is the unanimously projected baseline state. Existing default/current-only audit-profile gates still decide whether a new waiver suppresses code-net-new.
63	
64	Unmatched findings are excluded from the stable-entry array but MUST be retained in an explicit unmatched-occurrences array with findingId, ruleId, subjectId, subjectPath, severity and waived. A baseline cannot silently claim a complete correspondence population when that array or enumeration uncertainty is nonempty. Comparison reports a correspondence deficiency for affected gating rules and does not classify unmatched records as resolved, unchanged or code-net-new by guesswork. Known comparable regressions still fail. An unwaived unmatched gating occurrence fails current analysis, while audit can only report correspondence-indeterminate for it; it must not guess CODE-NET-NEW. Path-waiving the occurrence can make current analysis pass while audit remains correspondence-indeterminate. Missing fingerprint-only waiver matches cannot suppress unmatched occurrences. Baseline artifact2 and comparison result2 carry this addition; historical artifacts do not silently acquire an empty-array assertion. Fingerprint-targeted repair/review requires a stable matched target; unmatched findings stay inspectable by findingId and receive an explicit target-correspondence-unavailable refusal for fingerprint-targeted actions. No automatic source edit is authorized by this design work.
65	
66	Command envelopes and SARIF retain one result per finding3, including separate configurations and unmatched occurrences. SARIF can use findingId as run-local identity; only matched findings carry stable partialFingerprints. Baseline aggregation must never silently deduplicate visible finding occurrences. A renderer cannot turn indeterminate into pass.
67	
68	## 7. Complete replay criterion
69	
70	An independent evaluator receives admitted input closure and constructs every output from scratch: subject descriptors; per-rule enumeration; all program-predicate descriptors and witnesses; every predicate proof; matched fingerprint descriptors and full findings/parameter bytes; unmatched records; waiver membership; rule outcomes/deficiencies; execution deficiencies; full proof; evidence, seal, policy derivation and Run IDs. It may not read claimed findings/witnesses to select subjects, parameters, citations or output IDs. Input admission precedes replay; hashes alone do not establish owner admission.
71	
72	Compare C of the COMPLETE recomputed proof and every referenced output preimage and H identity with retained claims. Check exact reachable output-set equality so extra unreferenced semantic outputs cannot masquerade as evaluated findings. Counts, selected predicate fields, final verdict, or existence of a recomputed digest alone are insufficient. Discriminating controls must mutate same-count parameter values, citations, severity, waiver membership, enumeration, imported address and findings, independently remint all enclosing identities, and show semantic replay refusal rather than merely a stale hash. Positive graphs must retain the normative schema and all native principal/input bytes, admit under the actual owner closure, then pass complete replay. Report separately bounded shape/unit checks, complete graph admission and complete semantic replay.
73	
74	## 8. Source-specific deficiency and public fault accounts
75	
76	The schema's evaluator-deficiency-registry is closed by source and exact cause. Every import deficiency carries evidenceKind (the atom/declaration's actual kind) even when no wrapper exists; a missing import pointer is not needed to identify which required declaration it failed. Other sources carry evidenceKind=null. NativeCause is a separately typed nullable owner carrier and cannot widen DeficiencyV2. Required-execution `inputRefs` are the canonical set of the ExecutionInputsV1 ref plus each originating Coverage, inventory, or candidate ref from the internal requiredCellDeficiencies row, as specified in §9.6. Atom, enumeration, correspondence and required-import deficiency `inputRefs` follow §9.5. All non-null subject/predicate addresses belong to this rule's independent evaluation; cell-level execution deficiencies have null addresses. Required/optional relevance is derived from policy; no gating flag is accepted in a deficiency. The origin is recomputed during replay, not inferred from text prefixes.
77	
78	EVALUATION.WORK_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED is an indeterminate semantic disclosure with remedy to raise/narrow the admitted analysis work budget. 196	### 9.6 `proof.executionDeficiencies` — required-execution bridge
197	
198	`requiredCellDeficiencies` and `derivedAccounts` are **internal admission-result records**, not `evaluation-deficiency`. They may use internal `cause` tokens `native-work-incomplete` and `unsupported-typed`. Those tokens are **not** proof `cause` values.
199	
200	**Bridge (applied to every internal `requiredCellDeficiencies` row before proof emission):**
201	
202	1. `source` := `execution` (assessment layer for required execution cells; not a claim that the raw evidence provider is “execution”).
203	2. Let `d = row.deficiency` (the typed `DeficiencyV2` or `null` or enumeration-local `source-syntax-invalid`).
204	3. If `d` is a member of `x-opensip-evaluator-deficiency-registry.sources.execution`, proof `cause := d`. Else if `d` is `null` or `source-syntax-invalid`, proof `cause := required-cell-unsatisfied`. Else admission refuses `EVALUATOR_EXECUTION_CAUSE_UNREGISTERED` (not a semantic proof).
205	4. `nativeCause := row.nativeCause` (owner `NativeCause` or null; not unzipped from a later sibling).
206	5. `universe :=` that row's enumeration binding `universe` (64-hex suffix or null).
207	6. `subjectId` := null; `predicateId` := null; `evidenceKind` := null.
208	7. `inputRefs := Cset({XI} ∪ row.inputRefs)`. `XI` is committed execution-context. `row.inputRefs` are the originating Coverage, inventory, or candidate refs. `XI` does not replace them.
209	
210	Every native `DeficiencyV2` member is a member of both the execution and native cause registries. Native-registry evaluator diagnostics (`uncovered-expected-source-subject`, `coverage-unknown`, …) are atom/witness causes (§9.5), not `DeficiencyV2` carriers, and are not this bridge's `cause`. In particular `uncovered-expected-source-subject` is **not** registered under `sources.execution` and is **not** the carrier for a census-driven incomplete account: step 3's existing `null` → `required-cell-unsatisfied` route already carries that obligation, so no new vocabulary member is needed and none is added.

212	**The `null` route is load-bearing, not a fallback.** A required native account whose incompleteness is pure missing work — no returned partition, or expected subjects no partition covers — reaches step 2 with `d = null` by design (execution-inputs §5), and step 3 turns it into `required-cell-unsatisfied` with `nativeCause = null`, the binding `universe`, and `{XI} ∪ row.inputRefs`. The originating Coverage refs, when any exist, are still there. Any nonempty `proof.executionDeficiencies` makes the sealed verdict at least `indeterminate` (§9.6 close), so the required cell remains unsatisfied rather than silently becoming complete.

318	## Retained input selection and complete replay
319	
320	`evaluator_input_model.v3.py` reconstructs the composition inputs using the native/schema/identity owner's admitted closure. It reads no claimed finding, witness value or verdict. Every selected Plan import is an evaluation input, including a wrapper whose scope has no matching subject; omission is structural. A non-null ImportObservation member must agree with the same claim in its canonical payload: runtime window/population, test selection, history range endpoints. Observation kind must equal wrapper kind, and members inapplicable to that kind are null. Null is undisclosed information; it is not a contrary positive assertion and is never filled with a fictional observation. The canonical payload remains the owner of its own declared selection/range/window.
321	
322	Each atom is evaluated against the complete admitted evaluation input selection, retaining availability and empty-population inputs as well as hits. `predicate-witness` has no `inputRefs` field. That complete selection is projected onto every atomic `predicateProofs[].inputRefs` as specified in §9; boolean nodes take the canonical union of immediate children. Atom-model consumed-ref subsets are not evaluator3 proof fields. Coverage deficiencies retain their original native cause and source universe. Inputs are immutable preimages; a retained native extraction assertion remains provider evidence, and replay does not rerun a compiler to establish extraction truth.
323	
324	`evaluator_replay_model.v3.py` first admits the retained owner graph, reconstructs inputs, invokes the actual atom scanner and composes complete outputs. It compares every recomputed proof field and every output object/blob preimage, then independently reconstructs semantic evidence, seal and Run. It compares full finding identities, message/parameter bytes, severity, citations, waivers and enumeration outcomes, not counts. The authoritative evidence view set equals selected view inputs; its coverage set is the union of those views' coverage plus explicit admitted coverage inputs. Additional retained unreachable objects do not become authoritative findings.
325	
326	The synthetic reference harness uses a temporary graph only to open the legacy owner closure, whose API is Run-based. Its provisional outputs are discarded as semantic answers: reconstruction uses only Plan, execution and retained inputs. The exported positive Run is newly composed and must pass complete replay. Real extraction and platform qualification remain separate required work.
327	
328	The public `identity-model.v3.close_run` boundary invokes complete replay. Storage preparation/restoration and cache admission against an authoritative Run inherit that stronger check. `open_run_closure` is an internal owner-admission primitive; calling it alone is not a claim that evaluator3 output is correct. Intermediate cache-key construction remains possible before a Run and grants no authority.
329	
330	Every explicit coverage input must also belong to a selected admitted view, so the owner's coverage producer-admission and unresolved-edge accounting have run for it. A coverage wrapper by itself is not a substitute for that native view admission. The normalized scanner receives exact import wrappers plus separately derived import-scope and current/consumable maps from owner admission; those are host projections, not caller-supplied result flags.

1	# Evaluator3 fault boundaries
2	
3	An internal refusal is not itself a public D9 code. The host retains the originating boundary and applies the public route for that boundary. It does not infer origin from a filename, a retained-versus-live flag or a prefix in the error text. The closed condition/origin routes are in evaluator-fault-observation.schema.v3.json. The reference evaluator_fault_model.v3.py validates actual StepTermination and command-envelope3 owners; check-evaluator-faults.v3.py exercises all routes and envelope parity.
4	
5	The same reference admission can be invoked over newly returned producer data or retained data. Re-admitting retained producer data preserves the producer-contract meaning of a structural violation. A known external configuration remains external configuration. A host bug constructing its own internal layer is a host invariant fault, as in the inherited native public-route law.
6	
7	| Condition | Public meaning |
8	| --- | --- |
9	| Malformed external policy, emission selection or configuration | request-rejected, CONFIG.INVALID, existing CONFIG.INVALID detail |
10	| Well-formed prospective selection above a published limit | request-rejected, REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE; exact field/count/limit and narrowing remedy, before any Plan is minted |
11	| Invalid host-generated internal layer | operational-failed, SYSTEM.OUTCOME.ILLEGAL_STATE, host-invariant, existing HOST.INVARIANT_VIOLATED envelope detail |
12	| Provider omits a required inventory/result pointer, supplies a malformed outcome, or violates its Plan/stage/subject joins | operational-failed, PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION, provider-protocol; structural producer violation, including re-derivation over retained producer inputs |
13	| Referenced promised retained bytes are lost | the existing EvidenceUnavailable carrier: operational-failed, HOST.IO_FAILURE, host-io, evidence.missing plus the missing reference |
14	| Supplied bytes fail schema/identity admission | admission refusal under their actual external or producer boundary; never silently converted into a missing-byte observation |
15	| Complete semantic replay disagrees with an otherwise admitted sealed result | evidence.regeneration-mismatch under the retained regeneration boundary; a live first-party evaluator contradicting its own reconstruction is a host invariant fault |
16	| A complete output cannot fit the published array or canonical-byte bound | operational-failed, OUTPUT.SERIALIZATION_FAILED, output-serialization, EVALUATION.OUTPUT_BOUND_EXCEEDED; no truncated or empty substitute Run |
17	
18	A valid partial/unavailable inventory, missing optional evidence, unknown native sufficiency or bounded execution exhaustion is semantic evidence. It is retained as typed deficiencies and participates in the specified rule/execution aggregation. It is not malformed producer output merely because its value is indeterminate. A source manifest that fails parsing uses the enumeration-local source-syntax-invalid deficiency; it does not extend NativeCause or pretend the provider crashed.
19	
20	Pointer omission, promised-byte loss and supplied-byte invalidity are separate observations with different remedies. The adapter must preserve the typed upstream decision list and relevant reference, rather than flattening every refusal to HOST.IO_FAILURE or accepting an arbitrary public-detail string. Existing D9 class/error/exit mappings remain in force. The mandatory LIVE D9 successor-artifact obligation is not discharged by this design reference or by a passing route-control suite.
21	
22	## Typed observation, custody and public projection
23	
24	A host boundary records exactly one closed condition and its actual origin. The
25	record names the raw SHA-256 of the unmodified owner diagnostic artifact and a
26	relevant reference (required for pointer omission, promised loss and replay mismatch). The adapter checks the artifact bytes and retains
27	the entire observation. It does not parse exception text to establish origin,
28	discard nested owner decisions, or rename NativeCause as a public error code.
29	Re-admission preserves the original producer or external origin. An arbitrary
30	caller cannot turn a provider failure into a host I/O failure by supplying a
31	different origin; capture of that origin belongs to the host TCB.
32	
33	The 24 allowed condition/origin pairs are explicit in the schema registry.
34	Unsupported pairs refuse JSON Schema admission as well as routing. Valid semantic partial outcomes, ordinary unknown
35	predicates and exhausted logical analysis budgets are not members of this fault
36	condition enum. A prospective selection limit and an output serialization bound include the exact field,
37	observed count and maximum; observed must exceed maximum. The cross-field numeric
38	comparison is a reference admission rule; standard JSON Schema cannot express
39	arbitrary sibling integer inequality without a nonstandard extension. The prospective selection refusal precedes Plan construction. Output
40	serialization failure can follow a Plan but must not mint a substitute Run. Missing promised bytes and omitted required output pointers
41	require a nonempty reference and have different allowed origins. Both replay
42	mismatch origins require the affected Run reference; no anonymous regeneration
43	mismatch is admitted.
44	
45	EVALUATION.REQUIRED_OUTPUT_OMITTED identifies a missing required provider or host
46	output pointer on the public surface, retaining its exact reference.
47	Provider-return occupancy refusals use this existing boundary. Malformed
48	FactBatchV3 / OccupancyCompanionV1 / projected V2 is
49	`input-schema-invalid:provider-return`. Join, occupancy-conflict,
50	ephemeral-identity-conflict, unbound caller envelope, and unnegotiated V3
51	are `input-join-invalid:provider-return`. Both keep public detail
52	`EVALUATION.INPUT_REFUSED`. Host-authored mapping
53	(`PROVIDER_RETURN_HOST_AUTHORED`) is `host-internal` and
54	`HOST.INVARIANT_VIOLATED` and MUST NOT capture. Internal keys stay in
55	diagnostic bytes; they are not DomainDetailCode members and invent no D9
56	code. Missing token / empty companions is lawful occupancy-unknown, not
57	`required-output-pointer-omitted`. LIVE D9 successor-artifact remains a
58	future obligation. Origin is recorded on the fault observation after refusal;
59	it is not an admit parameter that blesses identical bytes.
60	
61	EVALUATION.INPUT_REFUSED preserves a structural evaluator input failure with
62	the exact diagnostic retained separately. EVALUATION.SELECTION_LIMIT names a
63	well-formed prospective request above the published bound.
64	EVALUATION.OUTPUT_BOUND_EXCEEDED names serialization failure. These are closed
65	DomainDetail codes registered in the common public registry; they create no
66	new D9 error code or exit code. The whole failure envelope carries the same
67	detail as StepTermination, and its exit code derives from termination.class.
68	Changing either side or reporting a different class's exit code refuses parity
69	admission. The earlier native owner may lawfully omit a domain detail; this
70	evaluator boundary supplies its own specifically registered detail.
71	
72	The retained-regeneration route agrees with identity's existing
73	RegenerationMismatch carrier (HOST.IO_FAILURE, host-io,
74	evidence.regeneration-mismatch). A live host evaluator contradiction is instead
75	host-invariant. A source failure does not make an admitted Run authoritative:
76	no failure envelope may replace a missing complete Run with an empty success.
77	
78	These bounded route controls are reference design evidence. The mandatory
79	LIVE D9 successor-artifact obligation and platform/host execution checks remain
80	separate implementation conformance requirements.
81	
82	## Native origin mapping and owner carriers
83	
84	The evaluator boundary uses its own closed origin vocabulary. Its schema's
85	`x-opensip-native-origin-map` explicitly maps the overlapping native boundaries:
86	external-configuration → external-configuration; external-specification →
87	externally-supplied-spec; host-internal → host-generated-internal-layer;
88	release-declaration → authenticated-release-declaration; provider-return →
89	producer-boundary. The evaluator-only retention, pre-Plan and serialization
90	origins have no native producer equivalent. Passing evaluator spellings directly
91	to the native public-route helper is not supported. This mapping preserves
92	boundary meaning, not equality of evaluator and native diagnostic detail codes.
93	
94	`owner_observation` accepts a typed retained owner carrier, retains opaque
95	diagnostic bytes and verifies the entire resulting termination, including
96	remedy and subject, against that carrier. It neither parses an exception
97	message nor substitutes a partially matching DomainDetail. The loss and
98	retained-regeneration routes use the existing identity remedies verbatim.

2	
3	This appendix is incorporated by product identity-and-evidence §4. It defines
4	`evaluator-projection-registry.v1.json`, `target-attribution.schema.v2.json`
5	(current selected attribution schema), `incoming-search.schema.v1.json`, and
6	`atom_model.v1.py`. Historical `target-attribution.schema.v1.json` remains a
7	retained document and is refused by this successor (`TARGET_ATTRIBUTION_SCHEMA_VERSION`).
8	Frozen24 remains replayable only under its own frozen selected V1 schema/profile.
9	Composition, proof, finding and gate rules are in the incorporated composition
10	contract. Complete Run admission combines these laws; atom checks alone are not
11	full replay. Acceptance and qualification are recorded separately.

13	Native fact payload `$defs` are not extended. Evaluator output profile remains 3:
14	evaluation-subject, finding3, proof3, and run3 recipes are unchanged.

18	## 1. Current subject
19	
20	*E* = (*U*, *K*, *N*) = `evaluation-subject` `{schemaVersion:3, universe, kind, nativeSubjectId}`. Kind is `file|symbol|package` and is required so a file path cannot collide with a package name.

File/symbol shape is unchanged: those kinds MUST NOT carry `packageManifestPath`. Native package scope membership remains `packageName`; the source atom additionally matches `payload.manifestPath` to `packageManifestPath`. Inventory identity/lookup does not collapse two manifests that share a name.

30	## 2. Target attribution
31	
32	Sidecar `TargetAttributionV2` is **provider attestation** captured as a host-derived typed input. Delivery is worker `OccupancyCompanionV1` on negotiated `FactBatchV3`, associated by `candidateOrdinal` before fact2 exists. `FactBatch.stageId` is C-2 text of the requested stage; host `DispatchBindingV1` carries `retainedStageOrdinal` separately because Analyze may be a subset of Plan stages. `buffer_fact_batch_occupancy` runs during ANALYZING (dispatch required; receipts/views not yet constructed). The host owning entry `bind_worker_occupancy` mechanically projects `TargetAttributionV2` after mint and `stageReceipt`, filling `planId` / `sourceFactId` / `producerClosure` from retained Plan, execution-plan stage spec, and selected views named on receipt `outputRefs`. Current-batch fact admission is separate from combined occupancy-conflict on `prior_records`. Missing token or empty companions is lawful occupancy-unknown except exact-id ephemeral. Host derivation is an **ephemeral projection on exact inventory native-id equality of `targetNativeId` only**. Host MUST NOT parse `SubjectIdV1` `namespace:opaque` spelling. `origin=host-internal` on a caller-built envelope refuses capture (`PROVIDER_RETURN_HOST_AUTHORED`).
33	
34	`evaluationNativeId` is the occupancy-compare field. It is required non-null iff `occupancy=first-party` and MUST be null otherwise. File: LogicalPath matching inventory `nativeSubjectId`. Package: attested `packageName`. Symbol: SubjectIdV1 MUST byte-equal `targetNativeId`. Malformed first-party sidecars (null `evaluationNativeId`, missing first-party `packageManifestPath`, nonunique/unadmitted inventory join) are **admission refusals**, not accepted unknown.

36	`packageManifestPath` is the sole package coordinate (no `evaluationPackageManifestPath`). Required non-null for `kind=package` and `occupancy=first-party` (inventory join of `(packageName=evaluationNativeId, path=packageManifestPath)`). Required non-null for `kind=package` and `occupancy=external` (query endpoint coordinate so GraphEndpoint `kind=package` is representable; not a first-party inventory join). MUST be null when occupancy=unknown or kind is not package.

40	Derivation uniqueness for **ephemeral** exact-id projection: DISTINCT admitted identities whose `nativeSubjectId` **exactly equals** payload `targetNativeId`. This is the existing symbol (and accidental C15 colon-path) authority. Size 0: ephemeral occupancy is not first-party. Absent sidecar then yields occupancy unknown, **not** payload-inequality nomatch.

42	Join refusals (sidecar vs independently known inventory): known kind mismatch; known exported mismatch; `occupancy=external` while ephemeral is first-party; `occupancy=first-party` while no unique inventory identity of `evaluationNativeId` (`TARGET_ATTRIBUTION_FIRST_PARTY_NOT_IN_INVENTORY`); independently known ephemeral first-party identity `I_eph` disagrees with sidecar first-party identity `I_sc` (`TARGET_ATTRIBUTION_EPHEMERAL_IDENTITY_CONFLICT` — C15 colon-path exact-id file vs a different same-kind inventory file; do not overwrite); schemaVersion≠2 (`TARGET_ATTRIBUTION_SCHEMA_VERSION`); sourceFact/plan/rung/producer joins including `TARGET_ATTRIBUTION_FIELD_NOT_ON_RUNG`. **Unknown sidecar fields cannot override known ephemeral fields.** Prefer independently known ephemeral fields; fill remaining unknown from sidecar.

Public standing is the existing evaluator-fault route: provider-emitted schema/join failures use `input-schema-invalid` / `input-join-invalid` with origin `provider-return` and public detail `EVALUATION.INPUT_REFUSED`; host-invented mapping uses origin `host-internal` and `HOST.INVARIANT_VIOLATED`. 56	## 3. Endpoints and filters
57	
58	Source occupancy uses the registered payload field (file `path`, package `packageName` **and** `manifestPath`, declares **`declared`** only — `container` is related, not a second occupancy and not a filter field). Absent field at the requested rung ⇒ filter forbidden at admission. Target occupancy at a **weaker** requested rung is refused even if a higher-rung fact has the resolved field.
59	
60	Incoming `subjectKind` projects the **SOURCE** endpoint’s inventory kind (importer/caller/referrer), not current `E.kind`.
61	
62	Runtime `subject` scalar: file → `row.path` (occupancy requires symbol absent); symbol → `row.symbol` (occupancy requires `path==inventory.path` ∧ `symbol==inventory.qualifiedName`). No concatenated path-and-symbol. Two matching rows in one wrapper refuse (ambiguity). Overload ambiguity (`FUNK` / `overload-ambiguous`) applies only when the **current** native ID is in the path/QN hit set of size > 1. An unrelated symbol not in that set is `nomatch` on the row; missing-observation uncertainty of that wrapper is retained and is not evidence about the unrelated symbol.
63	
64	**Universe filter:** closed enum of the three portable domains. Illegal values (hex, `sha256:`) refuse at admission. Valid domains use **normal** comparators: `neq` of two different valid domains is **true**. Projection is the selected **endpoint** universe’s portable domain. No H union.
65	
66	`exitStatus` null ⇒ unknown. Integer arrays for `exitStatus in` kept.

68	---
69	
70	## 4. Completeness partitions
71	
72	Obligations use the **exact requested rung**. Matching facts may use rung ≥ min. Higher-rung partial Coverage cannot block a complete requested rung.
73	
74	**Outgoing:** only scopes/coverages at exact rung whose associated scope **contains the current source subject**. Pairing is native `subject_scope_commitment` of the actual subject-scope2 descriptor (no invented `commitment` field) **or** explicit owner-derived `coverageScopes` mapping (root derives from the coverage envelope `scopeId`). No one-scope/one-coverage fallback. Each containing scope without a paired Coverage is `scope-without-coverage` even when another scope paired. Rule-level enumeration uncertainty is root, not this atom. Outgoing completeness is that *U*/source partition. An unrelated optional unavailable **same-family** program does not poison it (`unavailable-program-binding` is an incoming/global search concern; required execution is a separate account). Cross-family unavailable still discloses `cross-family-edge-not-owed` and is non-blocking.
75	
76	**Completeness result and its independence from truth.** The rules in this section compute a
77	**completeness result** `{complete, unknown, causes, coverageIds, scopeIds, nativeDeficiencies}`.
78	Where a rule below says **return**, it ends **only that completeness computation** with
79	`complete=false`, `unknown=true`, and the `causes`, `scopeIds` and `coverageIds` **accumulated so
80	far, retained exactly as they stand**. It does **not** end matching, and it does **not** by itself
81	decide the atom value. Matching facts and observations are collected independently and are never
82	discarded by a completeness return: a **known** match still makes `exists` **true**, `none`
83	**false**, and `count-at-most` **false** when the distinct known count exceeds *n* — §7's
84	"uncertain ids are retained even when a known value dominates" applies unchanged. Completeness only
85	decides whether the *remaining* value is the negative answer or `unknown`: with no dominating known
86	match, `exists` is `false` and `none` / `count-at-most` are `true` **only** when
87	`complete=true ∧ unknown=false` and no uncertain match exists; otherwise `unknown`.
88	
89	**Selection order (both endpoints).** Wherever this section selects several scopes or several
90	Coverage partitions, the selected list is ordered by **ascending scope2 / coverage2 identifier**,
91	and every first-wins fold below reads that order. The reconstructed scope and Coverage maps are
92	keyed collections with no inherent order, so without this rule a first-wins carrier would depend on
93	the host's map ordering rather than on the evidence.
94	
95	The order a fold reads is the order of the **final combined list**, after pairing and after
96	duplicate Coverage identifiers are removed. Coverage is reached *through* scopes — both the
97	current-source selection and the dependency selection walk containing scopes and collect each
98	scope's paired Coverage — so a per-scope walk hands the fold a **descending** Coverage order
99	whenever a scope with the lower identifier carries the Coverage with the higher one. Therefore:
100	**deduplicate the combined Coverage selection and sort it ascending by `coverage2` identifier;
101	do not rely on the scope walk to produce that order.** Scope order stays ascending `scope2`, which
102	is what orders `scopeIds` and decides which scopes are unpaired; Coverage order is decided only
103	after pairing. A Coverage paired by more than one containing scope appears **once**.
104	
105	**Cause representation (`universe`).** `AtomCauseV1` lists `universe` as an **optional, nullable**
106	property, and the atom record carries the key only when a cause has a universe to report. The
107	composition/replay projection reads it with a defaulting get and writes `evaluation-deficiency`,
108	whose `universe` is **required and nullable**, so an omitted atom key becomes an explicit `null`
109	there. Where this section writes `universe: null` it names that **logical, projected** value, not a
110	requirement that the atom record serialize an explicit null key; where it names a universe, the
111	atom record carries that string. Neither schema nor the projection recipe changes.
112	
113	**Shared prelude (both endpoints), before any endpoint-specific rule.** Let **owed bindings** be the
114	EnumerationPlan bindings for `capabilityForRelation[relation]` — the same set the incoming
115	paragraph below defines. A binding is **available** when its admitted `universe` coordinate is
116	non-null and **unavailable** when that coordinate is null; `UnavailableProgramBindingV1` fixes
117	`universe` to null, so an unavailable binding carries no universe to report. A binding's language
118	family is `engineFamilies.families[*].languageModes` of its cell `languageMode`, and a universe's
119	family is `engineFamilies.families[*].universeDomain`
120	(`evaluator-projection-registry.v1.json#/engineFamilies`). A family is **owed** for the subject
121	when either side is unknown or the two are equal.
122	
123	* **P1 — unavailable-binding scan.** For each **unavailable** owed binding: when its family is
124	  **not** owed for the subject's family, emit `cross-family-edge-not-owed` with `universe: null`
125	  — the binding's own coordinate — and take no further account of that binding. Otherwise, when the
126	  family **is** owed, emit `unavailable-program-binding` **only for `endpoint=target`**; outgoing
127	  emits nothing here, per the Outgoing paragraph above.
128	* **P2 — no owed binding at all**, neither available nor unavailable, for
129	  `capabilityForRelation[relation]`: emit `missing-relation-coverage`, `universe: null`, and
130	  **return** with empty `scopeIds` and empty `coverageIds`. **This return is shared — it is reached
131	  before the endpoint split, so incoming takes it on the same terms as outgoing.** P1 ran first but
132	  cannot have emitted anything on this path, because P2 requires that no unavailable binding exists.
133	
134	Because P1 precedes P2 and every endpoint-specific rule, a cross-family disclosure survives any
135	later return; since the scan reads the unavailable bindings, such a disclosure can co-occur with
136	every rule below but not with P2.
137	
138	**Outgoing cause derivation (`endpoint=source`), in order,** after the shared prelude:
139	
140	1. **Owed bindings exist but none available has `universe = U`**: emit `selector-unbound`,
141	   `universe: null`, and **return**. `scopeIds` and `coverageIds` are empty.
142	2. **No retained scope at exact `(relation, minResolution)` in *U* contains the current subject**:
143	   emit `uncovered-expected-source-subject`, `universe: U`, and **return**. `scopeIds` and
144	   `coverageIds` are empty.
145	3. Otherwise every containing scope is added to `scopeIds`. For **each** containing scope with no
146	   paired Coverage emit `scope-without-coverage`, `universe: U` — an unpaired scope is never
147	   skipped because a sibling scope paired. That describes **accumulation**; the returned `causes`
148	   is then deduplicated and ordered by §7 and the composition Cset law, where identical records
149	   collapse. What this rule fixes is that the cause is accumulated at all, and that `scopeIds`
150	   still names every containing scope. If any scope was unpaired, **or** no pairing was produced at
151	   all, **return**: `scopeIds` holds **every** containing scope and `coverageIds` is **empty**,
152	   because evaluation stops here without evaluating any paired sibling's Coverage. This is an
153	   outgoing rule only; it does not weaken the incoming accounting obligation stated below.
154	4. Otherwise, for each paired Coverage in selection order: add it to `coverageIds` and evaluate the
155	   shared sufficiency view (see the dependency paragraph below). When the view is not satisfied,
156	   emit `coverage-unknown` with `universe` = that Coverage's key `sourceUniverse` and the
157	   `nativeCause` the dependency paragraph selects. Evaluation continues to the remaining paired
158	   Coverage; step 4 has no return.
159	
160	**Incoming cause derivation (`endpoint=target`).** After the shared prelude — **including P2's
161	return, which incoming takes** — incoming makes **no further early return**: it accumulates across
162	every owed universe and provider and reports one completeness result at the end, which is what
163	"account **every** represented Coverage *S→V* **and every source scope**" below requires. Its first
164	accumulation is I1.
165	
166	* **I1 — the subject's own program is always an owed source.** The subject universe *U* is itself
167	  a source of incoming edges (*U→U*), whatever other programs are bound, so no incoming negative can
168	  stand unless *U*'s own referrers were accounted.
169	  **Precondition:** `endpoint=target`, P2 did not return, and **no available owed binding has
170	  `universe = U`** — the same test as outgoing step 1.
171	  **Emission:** `selector-unbound` with `evidenceKind: null`, `nativeCause: null` and `universe: null`
172	  (the projected value; the atom record omits the key) — exactly the record outgoing step 1 emits.
173	  The null is deliberate: no binding coordinate equal to *U* exists to attribute, *U* is already the
174	  atom subject's own coordinate, and naming *U* here would present a program that was never searched
175	  as an examined source partition.
176	  **Effect:** blocking — the completeness result is `complete=false`, `unknown=true` — but it is
177	  **not** a return. Every other owed universe and provider is still accounted and every cause it owes
178	  is still emitted, and matching is untouched, so a known match still decides `exists`, `none` and
179	  an exceeded `count-at-most` exactly as the completeness-result paragraph above states; only the
180	  answers that need completeness (`none`/`exists` without a known match, `count-at-most` not
181	  exceeded, `all-covered`) become `unknown`.
182	  **Precedence:** after P1 and P2, before the per-universe accumulation below. It is emitted at most
183	  once per evaluation and does not depend on binding, scope, Coverage, inventory or attestation order.
184	* **Unavailable bindings never satisfy I1.** An unavailable binding has `universe: null`, so it can
185	  never be the available binding at *U* that I1 requires. When an owed unavailable binding whose
186	  family is owed also exists, P1 has already emitted `unavailable-program-binding`; I1 emits
187	  `selector-unbound` beside it and both are retained.
188	* **Foreign-family-only obligations.** When every owed binding is of a family not owed for the
189	  subject — available, unavailable or both — I1's precondition holds, so the incoming answer is
190	  `unknown` with `selector-unbound`, and the `cross-family-edge-not-owed` disclosures of both routes
191	  below are retained beside it. Foreign-family work stays non-blocking in itself; what blocks is that
192	  the subject's own program was never searched.
193	* **Explicit selection scope.** An explicit request — `analysis.capabilities`, or any admitted
194	  analysis-spec whose ownership tuples omit the subject's unit for `capabilityForRelation[relation]`
195	  — is a visible, lawful narrowing of the **work requested**. It does not narrow what an incoming
196	  negative must have searched: such an atom answers `unknown` with `selector-unbound`, never a
197	  negative that cites only other programs' Coverage. I1 applies however the request was produced.

55	## 4. Cells, inventories, derived outcomes
56	
57	One outcome per enumeration `(cellOrdinal, programOrdinal)`. Inventory digests: **exactly one per kind**, kinds set-equal to the cell. Inventories are host-derived typed inputs (see §7); they are not checked as fictional stage outputs.
58	
59	**Outcome `state` is derived**, then joined to the host row:
60	
61	| Inputs | Derived `state` |
62	|---|---|
63	| enumerator unselected, or universe null | `unavailable` |
64	| selected U, typed provider-unavailable candidate/inventory, no returned work | `unavailable` (typed stage result allowed) |
65	| any inventory `partial`, or any supported-available account not complete | `partial` |
66	| all inventories complete, every account complete/inapplicable/unsupported, candidate complete if owed | `complete` |
67	
68	Partial inventory is legitimate known rows: the row is `partial`, not a structural refuse of the graph. `complete` + partial inventory is `EXECUTION_INPUTS_OUTCOME_DERIVE`. The row's deficiency/nativeCause **equals the derived primary pair** — the **first retained source that actually carries a typed pair**, in the cross-source order published immediately below — and that pair must actually occur on a source record — not an unzipped first-deficiency plus a later unrelated nativeCause, and not a rewrite of inventory `budget-exhausted` as generic `provider-unavailable`. When **no** retained source carries a pair (pure missing work), the derived pair is explicitly `(null, null)`; the row stays `partial` and nothing is manufactured (§5). Required partial inventory with otherwise complete native accounts still emits `required-cell-unsatisfied` with the inventory digest as `inputRef`. All originating causes and inputRefs are retained on `derivedOutcomes`. `requiredCellDeficiencies` and `derivedAccounts` are internal admission-result records, not schema `evaluation-deficiency`; they may use internal tokens `native-work-incomplete` / `unsupported-typed` that are not proof `cause` values. The proof bridge (composition §9.6) reads `row.deficiency` (a `DeficiencyV2`, `null`, or `source-syntax-invalid`), maps `null`/`source-syntax-invalid` to proof cause `required-cell-unsatisfied`, keeps `source=execution` as the required-execution assessment layer, and sets proof `inputRefs` to the canonical set of the ExecutionInputsV1 ref plus each originating `row.inputRefs`. Inventory failure originating refs are `subject-inventory` digests. Native-account failure originating refs are Coverage digests from `coverageRecords` (or named `coverageIds` when no records exist). Candidate failure originating refs are `candidate-producer-result` digests. The ExecutionInputsV1 ref is committed execution context, not a replacement for those originating refs. Empty `kinds` is not complete-empty work.

112	## 5. Native Coverage accounts (derived)
113	
114	Account fields are **references + explicit applicability**. Admission derives `accountState`, `coverage`, `resolutionCompletenessState`, `examinedExhaustive`, `deficiency`, **every** `nativeCause`, `scopeIds`, and **`coverageRecords`** from **all** owner `CoverageResultV3` entries of **this** cell/program's returned views, own enumerator/provider, U, and pair. Each coverage record keeps `deficiency+nativeCause+inputRef` together. No branch may unzip deficiencies and nativeCauses and re-pair the first of each.
115	
116	**Applicability is FIRST-MATCH, and the order is normative.** Exactly one token applies.
117	
118	| # | `applicability` | Matches when | `sourceUniverse` |
119	|---|---|---|---|
120	| 1 | `inapplicable-vcs` | relation is `vcs-change` **and** the admitted VCS observation `kind` is `none` | binding U |
121	| 2 | `unsupported-typed` | the matrix cell for `(capabilityId, languageMode)` is `UNSUPPORTED-TYPED` | binding U |
122	| 3 | `unavailable-unselected` | the binding enumerator `status` is `unselected` | binding U — always null here, see below |
123	| 4 | `unavailable-null-universe` | the binding `universe` is null | null |
124	| 5 | `supported-available` | otherwise | binding U |

126	Row 3 deliberately precedes row 4. `enumeration-contract.v1.md` §1 refuses a non-null universe on an
127	unselected enumerator, so an unselected binding always has `universe=null`; testing the universe first
128	would make `unavailable-unselected` **unreachable** and collapse two advertised enum members into one.
129	In this order they have distinct reachable meanings: **the enumerator was not selected** (an optional
130	`{status:"unselected", reason:"optional-unselected"}` binding), versus **a selected enumerator whose
131	binding has no universe** (an unavailable binding — pre-Plan input or provider unavailable). Row 2
132	outranks both, so an `UNSUPPORTED-TYPED` cell still discloses its matrix deficiency and that
133	deficiency's registered cause even when the enumerator is unselected and U is null. A malformed
134	binding shape is rejected by **its own owner**; no shape is ever constructed here solely to reach a
135	branch.
136	
137	**`sourceUniverse` is the binding's universe coordinate — an EXTERNAL join.** For **every**
138	applicability, `nativeCoverageAccounts[i].sourceUniverse` **equals**
139	`EnumerationPlanV1.cells[cellOrdinal].programBindings[programOrdinal].universe`. Carrying no Coverage
140	does **not** erase that coordinate: an `inapplicable-vcs`, `unsupported-typed` or unavailable account
141	still belongs to the universe its binding names. A **null binding U remains null**. The competing rule

143	normative one is published here instead of living only in the reference implementation. Violation is
144	`EXECUTION_INPUTS_COVERAGE_DERIVE`.

146	JSON Schema **cannot** state this: the comparand is a different document. `NativeCoverageAccountV1`
147	therefore publishes the join as `x-opensip-external-joins` and the precedence as

485	**A scope is judged on ITS OWN extent where the published law supplies one.** The
486	relation registry states, per relation, what `subject-scope.subjects` identify

498	symbols to files is **trusted** and is not re-derivable from the retained Run, so
499	the only answerable question is the coarser one — can this universe produce this

501	a symbol identifier as a path would reject lawful code scopes, and inventing

505	
506	**Path support is decided by the SELECTED grammar ROWS and their own suffixes**,
507	not by the set of selected languages. The descriptor permits a row to own a
508	**subset** of its language's bundled suffixes, and two rows of one language may
509	own disjoint suffixes; admission requires only that a claimed suffix belong to
510	that language and that no suffix be claimed twice. A selected TypeScript row
511	owning `.ts` therefore establishes nothing about a `.tsx` path when no selected
512	row owns `.tsx`, and longest match runs over the union of the selected rows' own

514	fact is **not** vacuously supported: it names no file that could have been read.

517	sources `typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/allowJs` and `/checkJs`, read 2026-09-06).
518	`allowJs` is a *program-membership* option: it admits JavaScript roots. `checkJs`
519	is a *diagnostics* option: it reports errors in JavaScript files and changes
520	nothing about what is resolved. Both are universe keys (they change PlanId);
521	neither gates a capability, and neither implies that resolution was attempted or
522	complete. Resolution completeness is asserted only by `CoverageResultV3` (§4.3).
523	The universe carries `jsAdmittedToProgram`, `jsDiagnosticsEnabled` and the
524	constant `resolutionCompletenessImplied=false` so no consumer can confuse them.

529	is an unresolved edge (§4.4), never a silent drop.
