566	### 1.4 Mixed repositories and workspace units (R1)
567	
568	The v1 rule ("deepest root, then `Cargo.toml` > `tsconfig.json`") was wrong: in a
569	repository whose root holds both `Cargo.toml` and `package.json`/`tsconfig.json`
570	every TypeScript file fell into the Rust unit and silently left the TypeScript
571	program. Units are now **per language family and program membership**, and may
572	share a root.
573	
574	**Reference discovery model** (`discover_units`, `assign_membership` in the model;
575	records `WorkspaceUnitV2`, `FileMembershipRowV1`, `UnitMembershipV1`). The root
576	discovery boundary and trust decision remain the security/foundation owners'
577	(DR-103); this contract defines what happens inside that boundary.
578	
579	`WorkspaceUnitV2` (closed): `{unitOrdinal, rootPath, languageFamily: rust|tsjs|none,
580	languageMode, unitKind: cargo-workspace|cargo-package|ts-program|js-program|syntax-only,
581	markerPath, markerSha256, recognizerId, recognizerVersion, provenance:
582	EXPLICIT|DISCOVERED|DEFAULTED, memberPackageRoots[]}`.
583	
584	- **U-0 (internal root representation, normative)** `rootPath` and every
585	  `memberPackageRoots[]` entry are the **internal** relative directory form and nothing
586	  else. `rootPath` is the empty string `` for the project root, or a canonical relative
587	  directory (`#/$defs/InternalUnitRootV1`); a member package root is always a NON-EMPTY
588	  canonical relative directory (`#/$defs/CanonicalRelativeDirV1`), because a member is
589	  always strictly inside its workspace root. A canonical relative directory is one or more
590	  `/`-joined non-empty segments with no leading or trailing `/`, no empty segment, no `.`
591	  or `..` segment, no NUL and no backslash. `CanonicalPath` is deliberately NOT this
592	  grammar: it admits a trailing `/` and an interior empty segment (`a//b`), neither of
593	  which is canonical for a directory used as a membership prefix.
594	  `.` is the **external** sentinel only, on both edges: Config2 `discovery.workspaceRoots`
595	  and CLI `--workspace-root` inbound (`normalize_explicit_root`, `.` -> ``), and the
596	  outward `workspaceRoot` of the shared scope record and of enumeration cells
597	  (`spell_root`, `` -> `.`). A retained `WorkspaceUnitV2` is **never** normalized after
598	  retention, because `rootPath` is consumed as an exact string prefix by U-3 membership, by
599	  relative-path slicing and by the deepest-unit `len(rootPath)` ranking.
600	  A unit whose root is not in internal form is refused **before** membership, slicing or
601	  enumeration binding reads it (`admit_unit_roots`; internal decision key
602	  `NATIVE_UNIT_ROOT_REPRESENTATION`, and `ENUMERATION_MEMBERSHIP_UNIT_ROOT` when the same
603	  decision is reached through enumeration admission). This is an INTERNAL host-invariant
604	  decision and adds no public detail code; a malformed EXTERNAL root keeps its existing
605	  typed public refusal `native.explicit-root-grammar` (CONFIG.INVALID). Deciding it first
606	  is the whole point: `.` makes every U-3 prefix test false, so the unit would silently own
607	  no file and the result would be an empty but schema-valid analysis, and the enumeration
608	  join would otherwise surface the same wrong root as `ENUMERATION_BINDING_PROGRAM_ENTRY`,
609	  attributing it to a different field.
610	- **U-1 (one unit per directory and language family)** A directory holding
611	  `Cargo.toml` yields a `rust` unit; a directory holding `tsconfig.json`,
612	  `jsconfig.json` or `package.json` yields exactly one `tsjs` unit whose mode is
613	  chosen by precedence `tsconfig.json` (→ `ts-tsconfig`/`js-allowjs`) >
614	  `jsconfig.json` (→ `js-allowjs`) > `package.json` (→ `js-synthesized`). The
615	  precedence selects the mode **within** `tsjs`; it never removes the co-located

795	**The capability vocabulary, its authority and its spelling (CB4-SHOULD-2).**
796	`analysis-spec.requestedCapabilities[].capabilityId` was `$ref: Text` and enters
797	`PlanId` through `analysisSpecDigest`, and no document named the vocabulary it is
798	drawn from. Three spellings were consequently in live use in one release: the
799	reference default-selection corpus emitted `relation@rung`
800	(`clones@normalized-body-hash`), the foundation reference fixture emitted a bare
801	relation name (`references`), and the capability matrix publishes `inventory`,
802	`syntax`, `clones-fact`, `clones-near`, `clones-cross-tsjs`, `unresolved-edge`.
803	Two conforming hosts requesting the same analysis of the same unit therefore mint
804	different `analysisSpecDigest`s, different `PlanId`s and different `RunId`s, which
805	defeats independent replay across machines. The `languageMode` sibling was
806	already closed against a registered map at Run closure; the capability was not.
807	
808	- **Authority.** `native/native-capability-matrix.v2.json#/capabilities[].id`,
809	  closed at eleven members, with the law published beside it at
810	  `#/capabilityIdLaw`. The same vocabulary serves
811	  `product-configuration.analysis.capabilities`, whose item pattern
812	  `^[a-z][a-z0-9._:-]*$` already contained no `@` — so the `relation@rung`
813	  spelling was never admissible at the configuration layer and is now refused by
814	  shape at the analysis-spec layer too, before membership is consulted.
815	- **A capability id is not a `relation@rung`.** They are different concepts and
816	  are not equated. A capability is a *requestable unit of work* and may cover
817	  several relations (`inventory` covers `file@enumerated`,
818	  `package@manifest-declared` and `vcs-change@vcs-reported`; `syntax` covers the
819	  three syntactic rungs) or none at all (`clones-near` and `clones-cross-tsjs`
820	  are candidate-only and bear no fact relation). A `relation@rung` is a
821	  *fact/Coverage coordinate*: it is what `CoverageKeyV2`, the §1.3 table, the
822	  grammar-capability registry and the relation ladders speak. The bridge in both
823	  directions is the matrix's own `capabilities[].relations`, so an implementer
824	  never has to guess one from the other.
825	- **Mode applicability.** A request names a capability *and* a `languageMode`.
826	  The `(capability, mode)` cell must exist — the table is the complete product of
827	  the eleven capabilities and the six modes, so it always does for registered
828	  members — and its state must not be `NOT-SELECTED`, which means "outside D-371;
829	  no promise" and is an *unsatisfiable* request rather than a disclosable one.
830	  An `UNSUPPORTED-TYPED` cell is a different thing entirely: it **is**
831	  requestable and is answered with `unknown` plus its own named deficiency and
832	  cause, never refused. Today's three `NOT-SELECTED` cells are
833	  `clones-cross-tsjs` under `rust-cargo`, `rust-cargo-prepared` and `syntax-only`.
834	- **The release declaration registry.** Its *content* stays an authenticated
835	  input — which rows a release ships is not a contract constant — but its schema
836	  (`native-evidence.schemas.v2.json#/$defs/ReleaseCapabilityRegistryV1`, rows
837	  `{capabilityId, languageModes[]}`), its membership authority (`capabilityId` ∈
838	  the matrix ids; every mode registered with a cell that is not `NOT-SELECTED`),
839	  its canonical spelling and its binding to the Plan are normative. A duplicate
840	  `capabilityId` refuses rather than merging, because two rows declaring
841	  different applicable modes for one capability would leave default selection
842	  ambiguous.
843	- **The analysis-spec ownership tuple is unique (CB8-SHOULD-2).** The rule above
844	  is the *release declaration's*; the **request** had no analogue, and it needed
845	  one for exactly the same reason. Within one analysis spec,
846	  `(capabilityId, languageMode, workspaceRoot)` **names one cell of work for one
847	  unit**, and `required` is that cell's **attribute**, not part of its name. Two
848	  rows over one tuple disagreeing only on `required` were admitted by the schema —
849	  `uniqueItems` sees two *distinct* items — and by the per-row vocabulary
850	  admission, which judges each row alone; and both entered `analysisSpecDigest`
851	  and therefore the `PlanId`, so the contradiction was **committed** rather than
852	  transient. Requiredness decides whether a missing Coverage entry contributes
853	  `indeterminate`, so an undetermined value there is not cosmetic. Such a spec is
854	  **refused**: there is deliberately no last-wins, no order dependence and no
855	  merge of requiredness, and a caller states one value per cell or the record is
856	  refused. The same `capabilityId` on a **different** `workspaceRoot` or a
857	  different registered `languageMode` is a different cell and remains legal, and
858	  different capabilities on one unit remain legal. In an **explicitly supplied**
859	  spec a **byte-identical** duplicate row is a different defect and keeps its own
860	  earlier answer — `uniqueItems` and the canonical-set order law refuse it at
861	  `validate_foundation`, before this rule is reached — so on that path this rule
862	  owns only distinct rows over one tuple. On the **default-construction** path the
863	  guard described below runs first and reports byte-identical rows under this same
864	  key; both paths name the same tuple. The law is published in the record's owning schema
865	  (`foundation/identity-schemas.v3.json#/$defs/analysis-spec`,
866	  `x-opensip-uniqueness`) and enforced in `admit_requested_capabilities`, the one
867	  helper that **both** the pre-Plan analysis-spec boundary **and** retained Run
868	  closure call, so the two boundaries agree by construction. It is a *determinacy*
869	  law and therefore belongs in that shared helper, unlike the population
870	  **cardinality** bound, which is a pre-Plan request-selection concern and stays at
871	  the request boundary; §10 keeps that cardinality-first special route unchanged.
872	  Its internal key `native.requested-capability-duplicate-ownership-tuple` is
873	  registered in the §10 route registry as **origin-dependent** over the existing
874	  external-configuration / externally-supplied-spec / host-generated-internal-layer
875	  routes, and it adds **no** public `DomainDetailCode` member. Default construction
876	  reports the **same** key. The matrix-fixed default emits unique tuples, and two
877	  co-located units in one mode produce byte-identical rows that
878	  `default_capability_selection` refuses rather than silently deduplicating, so no
879	  requested analysis is lost. That guard runs **before** the analysis-spec boundary

880	  — `uniqueItems` would otherwise answer with a generic schema error restating the
881	  whole instance, the same reason the §10 cardinality guard precedes generic
882	  validation — and it names this registered key, not a private one. An earlier
883	  revision raised a bespoke `DUPLICATE_REQUESTED_CAPABILITY` there, which had **no**
884	  row in the §10 route registry: `public_termination_for` refused it
885	  (`native.public-route-key-unregistered`), so this duplicate-selection refusal had no derivable
886	  public termination, even though this key's
887	  host-generated route was written for exactly that call site. The refusal, its
888	  position and its non-deduplicating behaviour are unchanged; only the key it names
889	  is, and no public `DomainDetailCode` member is added for it.
890	
891	**The registry states availability; it never states scope.** An earlier revision
892	said "the registry may declare a **subset** of the matrix — a release need not
893	ship everything". That sentence was written about *membership* and reads as
894	permission about *scope*, and it is corrected here, because the default was
895	driven **from** the registry: a staged build shipping three rows silently
896	requested three capabilities and still looked conformant. That is the D-371
897	selected product quietly shrinking with nothing disclosed anywhere, against this
898	section's own promise that the default is the full registered set and against
899	admission §1.1's complete intended product.
900	
901	- **Required default (fixed by the matrix, not by a release).** For each
902	  discovered unit the `default` profile **must** request every capability whose
903	  `(capability, unit languageMode)` cell is not `NOT-SELECTED` — the published
904	  definition of the selected product, since `NOT-SELECTED` means "outside D-371;
905	  no promise". `UNSUPPORTED-TYPED` cells are **included deliberately**: the matrix
906	  says such a cell "refuses with the named deficiency; never silently narrows",
907	  and the way it never silently narrows is that the default asks and the Run
908	  answers with the disclosed unavailable pair. Omitting it would leave a consumer
909	  with no record that the capability exists and was not served.
910	- **Absence is disclosed, not dropped — and delivered.** A capability the product
911	  requires and this release does not declare available is still requested, and the
912	  selection boundary records the absence in `default_capability_selection`'s
913	  `undeclaredCapabilities`. That record is an **availability account, not a
914	  `CoverageResultV3`** and not a final `(deficiency, nativeCause)` pair — and, on
915	  its own, it is a helper return, not something a consumer receives. An earlier
916	  revision stopped there and called it "machine-readable"; an in-memory result is
917	  not a delivered disclosure.
918	- **The public carrier, named — and it delivers in *this* invocation.** One
919	  analysis step's selection produces the `{noticeCount, notices[]}` leaf
920	  (`release_absence_notices`); adding its `stepId` forms a
921	  `CapabilityAvailabilityStepV1`, and the invocation's steps compose
922	  `CapabilityAvailabilityV1` = `{stepCount, totalNoticeCount, steps[]}`
923	  (`invocation_availability`), carried on **`CommandEnvelope.availability`**.
924	  Each notice carries the **complete ownership tuple in typed fields** —
925	  `capabilityId`, `languageMode` and the unit's own `workspaceRoot` — with the
926	  code `native.capability-unavailable` and the registered remedy. Two things this
927	  fixes: an earlier revision concatenated `<capabilityId> @ <languageMode>` into
928	  a `subject` and **discarded `workspaceRoot`**, so two units requesting the same
929	  capability collapsed into one indistinguishable notice; and it had no carrier
930	  for *multiple* absences in the original invocation at all, since
931	  `StepTermination.domainDetail` is singular and a `doctor` report is a
932	  **different invocation**. The tuple is never concatenated: `workspaceRoot` is a
933	  `UserInputPath` bounded at 4096 while `BoundedText` is 1024, so concatenation
934	  could silently truncate a path.
935	- **Composed per step, because 1024 is the analysis-spec bound.** Each analysis
936	  step's own selection becomes a `CapabilityAvailabilityStepV1`
937	  (`{stepId, noticeCount, notices[≤1024]}`), and the invocation carries
938	  `{stepCount, totalNoticeCount, steps[≤64]}`. A *step's* collection cannot
939	  truncate — 1024 is exactly the `analysis-spec.requestedCapabilities` bound and
940	  one selection yields at most one absence per requested row — but the invocation
941	  is **not** bounded by that number: a named multi-step invocation carries up to
942	  64 steps, and two admitted selections of 1023 requests each compose 2046
943	  notices, which one flat 1024 array refused. Composing per step preserves every
944	  valid admitted invocation and **discards no notice to fit**; `steps` is bounded
945	  by the invocation's own step bound (`StepId` 0–63).
946	- **Association, order and count.** Each entry names the `stepId` whose selection
947	  produced it. A step that made **no** selection contributes no entry; a step
948	  that selected and found nothing absent contributes an entry with an **empty**
949	  array, which is the positive statement that it checked; a retried step
950	  contributes one entry, for the attempt whose selection the invocation retained.
951	  The same ownership tuple may recur in **different** steps, so uniqueness is
952	  within a step and never across the invocation. `noticeCount` equals each step's
953	  array length and `totalNoticeCount` is their sum — stated invariants, not a
954	  truncation policy. Order is the selection's own, under
955	  `x-opensip-order: sequence`. `AnalysisResult` is a closed union and is **not**
956	  widened.
957	- **The notice's code is its condition.** `code` is `const
958	  native.capability-unavailable`, not the whole `DomainDetailCode` enum: this
959	  typed record declares exactly one condition, and an earlier revision admitted
960	  `CONFIG.INVALID` on a release-absence notice.
961	- **Declared parity, not merely envelope membership.** Being present on the
962	  envelope does not make a field part of renderer parity — `render` selects only
963	  a command's declared `parityFields`, so the collection reached JSON and agent
964	  and was omitted by human, SARIF and HTML. `capability-availability` is now a
965	  declared parity field of every `requestClass: analysis` command (`default`,
966	  `analyze`, `fit`, `audit`, `repair-verify`), so every applicable renderer
967	  carries it.
968	- **Authority limits.** The disclosure is **advisory**: it terminates nothing,
969	  mints no Coverage, creates no Control verdict and no repair authority, and
970	  fabricates no clone `Candidate` — the published Candidate records represent
971	  actual candidates, so an absent provider can never be one. Nothing here
972	  truncates: a step's `notices` is bounded by the analysis-spec request bound it
973	  can never exceed, and `steps` by the invocation's own step bound, so
974	  `noticeCount` and `totalNoticeCount` are exact rather than a residue of a
975	  dropped tail.
976	- **Which capabilities use which route.** A **fact-producing** capability keeps
977	  its `relation@rung` Coverage under the existing precedence, and this detail
978	  does not replace it. A **candidate-only** capability has no Coverage entry at
979	  all, so this detail is its *only* public route. No new vocabulary, no new
980	  public code, **no preview or default exception**.
981	- **What an absence projects to, and what wins when two apply.** Neither case may
982	  be assumed. *Precedence*: a capability can be undeclared **and** unservable by
983	  the admitted universe at once — `references` under `syntax-only` is both. The
984	  syntax capability prerequisite *derives* `language-tier-unsupported` /
985	  `capability-missing` for such a scope and refuses anything else, and §10's
986	  precedence ranks `language-tier-unsupported` ahead of `provider-unavailable`,
987	  so the more specific one wins and the release-absence account never overrides
988	  it. Where no more specific deficiency applies, `provider-unavailable` with
989	  `capability-missing` is the applicable pair on the existing
990	  `COVERAGE.PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` route. *Candidate-only capabilities*:
991	  `clones-near` and `clones-cross-tsjs` have **empty** matrix `relations` — they
992	  are candidate-only by §6.1 authority, mint no fact and no `relation@rung`, and
993	  therefore have **no Coverage entry** that could carry a pair; requiring one
994	  would mean fabricating a relation. Their account is the selection record itself
995	  (`projection: selection-account-only`), while fact-producing capabilities carry
996	  `projection: coverage-entry` and name the exact `relation@rung` coordinates
997	  they project onto. An availability account may be shared by all capabilities;
998	  it is automatically a Coverage result for none of them.
999	- **Availability is not qualification.** Declaring a capability cannot promote a
1000	  cell: `platformQualified` stays false, no cell is `QUALIFIED`, and
1001	  `SUPPORTED-DESIGN` remains "contracted behavior, corpus named, qualification
1002	  pending" whatever a release declares. A staged or development build shipping
1003	  fewer providers is an availability fact disclosed per request — not a narrowed
1004	  product and not a completed release qualification.
1005	- **Explicit configuration overrides the request, not the obligation.**
1006	  `product-configuration.analysis.capabilities` uses this same vocabulary; an
1007	  override is a recorded choice with its own provenance (the default's is
1008	  `DEFAULTED`). A user narrowing their own analysis is visible; a host silently
1009	  narrowing the product would not be.
1010	- **The host input boundary, honestly.** *Which* rows a release ships is an
1011	  authenticated input this contract cannot measure, and nothing here qualifies a
1012	  build, an installer or a provider. What is contract is the obligation the
1013	  default must meet, the membership the declaration is held to, and the
1014	  disclosure an absence owes.
1015	- **Closed at admission, not only in the helper.** The default helper is one
1016	  producer of an `analysis-spec`, not the authority. The same vocabulary is
1017	  closed again at Plan/Run closure over the **retained** `analysis-spec`
1018	  (`ANALYSIS_SPEC_CAPABILITY:native.requested-capability-*`), so an explicitly
1019	  configured or hand-built spec is judged by exactly the rule a defaulted one is,
1020	  and the default and explicit paths agree on one spelling by construction. The
1021	  foundation keeps its own fault for an unregistered *mode*; native owns which
1022	  capabilities exist and which cells this product promises anything for.
1023	
1024	No capability is added, removed or renamed, no cell state changes, and all six
1025	advertised modes, the three native contexts and the full default-selected
1026	product stay exactly as representable as before. What is new is the authority
1027	for a field that had none.
1028	
1029	**Plan-bound evaluator parameters are not stuffed into the pre-Plan capability
1030	helper.** `default_capability_selection` emits the complete capability REQUEST
1031	(`defaultIsCompleteCapabilitySelection`) and an analysis-spec with
1032	`parameters: []` **by design**: it runs before snapshot, scope and membership
1033	exist. That flag is complete capability-request selection, not a complete
1034	evaluator3 spec. For evaluator3, a later host Plan-construction stage commits
1035	exactly one `EnumerationPlanV1` and exactly one `EvaluatorEmissionPlanV1` as
1036	`analysis-spec.parameters` (identity §4; identity-schemas.v3
1037	`requiredForEvaluatorMajors=[3]`). Those records are Plan-bound configuration:
1038	they are not fields of `product-configuration.schema.v2`, they do not execute
1039	code, and this helper does not mint them. Generic payload-registry cardinality
1040	still allows zero entries for a row a *different* consumer does not need. The
1041	execution-inputs manifest then accounts every selected cell's required work
1042	over the independently retained census. Required cells remain required when
1043	rules are disabled or no subjects match. A missing expected inventory pointer
1044	is structural refusal, not a manufactured empty population.
1045	
1046	**Backup custody join.** Dependency-source files, inert prepared rows and
1047	generated-file blobs are host CAS objects under the one host storage root; they
1048	inherit the identity-and-evidence §5 backup-managed-storage choice
1049	(`--allow-backup-custody` or an admitted storage-policy record; CI without a
1050	choice refuses `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED` / `storage.backup-choice-required`).
1051	Native adds no second store and no custody rule of its own.

505	`partial-acceptable` at least one. That enum already existed, but **this reading of

509	test fails* — it does not veto a lawful `partial-acceptable` requirement that has a

511	window or revision range applies under both completeness values, because it is a
512	property of the observation rather than of the target count. And **required versus
513	optional** stays where `evidenceUse` puts it — an optional absence remains the
514	`IMPORT.ABSENT_FOR_PREDICATE` disclosure and is satisfied *by absence* rather than
515	by evidence. That declaration reaches the requirement boundary as a **typed

517	falsy value is read as optional.

521	## 5. Declarative policy DSL, authoring test, candidate → inspect → review
522	
523	**DSL.** `PolicyDocumentV2` is closed data: rules with a `ruleProgramRef`
524	(contribution, stable id, semantics major, program digest), `enabled`, `severity`
525	(`note|warning|error`), `gate`, a `subjectEnumeration` (universe, subject kind,
526	include/exclude globs over `LogicalPath` with only `*`, `?` and whole-segment `**`),
527	an `emitWhen` predicate tree and `evidenceUse` declarations. Predicates are exactly
528	the evaluator's set: atoms `exists|none|count-at-most|all-covered` over a relation,
529	minimum resolution and typed field filters (`eq|neq|in|prefix|glob|gte|lte`), plus
530	`and|or|not`, depth ≤ 8, ≤ 64 nodes per rule, ≤ 512 rules. Evaluation is strong
531	Kleene: under incomplete Coverage `exists` is true on a match else indeterminate,
532	`none` false on a match else indeterminate, `count-at-most` false above N else
533	indeterminate, `all-covered` indeterminate. A true predicate emits a finding; false
534	is a retained no-match; an indeterminate gating rule is a typed deficiency. An atom
535	over imported evidence must be declared in `evidenceUse`; required evidence absent
536	makes the rule indeterminate, optional evidence absent is disclosed as
537	`IMPORT.ABSENT_FOR_PREDICATE` and is not a gating deficiency. There is no string
538	expression, hook, script, include or exec key; any such key is a schema violation
539	(`POLICY.IMPERATIVE_KEY_REFUSED`). Policy, ScopeDocumentV1 and resolved WaiverSetV1
540	digests are raw SHA-256 of their canonical closed documents, retained as blobs.
541	
542	Glob matching follows the single [portable glob contract](../../../coop/design-corrections/foundation/glob-pattern-contract.v1.md): full-string, case-sensitive matching; terminal whole-segment `**` includes a filename, so `src/**` matches `src/index.ts`. The same predicate applies to policy field filters and host path scopes. Each containing contract continues to own its defaults and include/exclude combination law.
543	The compiled RuleProgramV2 separately hashes its policy digest and ordered rule
544	programs to proof.ruleProgramDigest; these are auxiliary hashes, not H identities.
545	The exact endpoint, native field projection and imported test-filter grammars
546	are in that policy schema and the incorporated atom contract. Identity §4 and
547	the composition contract own independent subject enumeration, complete tree
548	replay, full finding emission, waiver membership and budget semantics. Declared
549	required evidence remains distinct from retained nonblocking branch diagnostics.
550	
551	**Waivers.** A waiver targets a fingerprint or `(ruleId, subjectPath)` with a reason
552	and `expires` (date or null). Expiry and duplicates are resolved at **Plan
553	construction** against the admitted trust clock: expired waivers leave the effective
554	set and are disclosed (`POLICY.WAIVER_EXPIRED`), two waivers on one target refuse
555	(`POLICY.DUPLICATE_WAIVER`, `CONFIG.INVALID`), and the Plan's `waiverDigest` is that of
556	the *resolved* effective set, keeping evaluation pure. `opensip waive` is the explicit
557	tracked-intent write; nothing writes a waiver implicitly.
558	
559	**Authoring test.** `opensip policy test SUITE` is Query class. A suite supplies the
560	candidate policy, waivers, an `asOfDate`, optional test-only overrides and cases with
561	typed fact fixtures (subjects, facts, declared Coverage, available evidence kinds) or
562	a bounded source fixture. Facts cases are evaluated by the deterministic fixture
563	verifier (the finite declarative fixture evaluator; this is reference evidence, not
564	qualification of the production evaluator or native providers); sources cases run only under an ephemeral non-authoritative Plan with
565	bundled providers and otherwise report `not-executable`. Expectations are
566	`finding{ruleId,minCount,maxCount,subjects}`, `no-finding`, `verdict`, `indeterminate`.
567	The result (`policytest2:`) records candidate and effective digests, resolver
568	acceptance and refusals, applied overrides, waiver resolution and
569	`enforcementUnchanged=true`; the same suite always yields the same result identity.
570	
571	**Candidate → inspect → review (Map side).** `opensip candidates` lists
572	`Candidate` records derived from one sealed Run: findings plus advisory kinds
573	(`clone-candidate`, `low-confidence-unused`, `runtime-unhit`, `history-stale`) with an
574	evidence level. Only a finding on a gating rule is `controlBearing`. `opensip inspect`
575	returns a bounded `InspectionBundle` (≤ 4096 facts, Coverage, imports, limitations).
576	`opensip review join` records a `ReviewDisposition` (`accept|reject|defer`, reviewer
577	principal human/model/policy-rule, note, `suppressUntil` ≤ 365 days) as a mutation
578	with a receipt. The disposition schema admits no verdict, Run, baseline or
579	authorization field: review can never mint a Control verdict or authorize a repair.
580	`reject`/`defer` suppress the candidate from listings until `suppressUntil` or until
581	its fingerprint changes; expired suppressions resurface with `previouslyReviewed`.
582	`opensip review brief` is an advisory, bounded (≤ 1000) ordering labelled with its
583	producer (a model producer names its `closure2`); truncation is explicit.

587	## 6. Repair preview, apply, verify (AR-08)
588	
589	Three separately authorized steps; schemas in `repair.schema.json`.
590	
591	**Preview** (`repair-preview`, Query class) requires an **authoritative** evidence Run
592	(`REPAIR.EVIDENCE_RUN_NOT_AUTHORITATIVE` for ephemeral) whose availability is retained
593	and whose sealed assurance is replayable (else the plan is not applicable with
594	`REPAIR.EVIDENCE_RUN_UNAVAILABLE`), a recipe closure admitted under current trust
595	(`REPAIR.RECIPE_TRUST_REVOKED`; an absent admission is also refused), targets present in that Run, and a live tree equal to
596	the Run's snapshot (`REPAIR.SOURCE_MOVED`). It emits `RepairPlanV1`

605	
606	**The closed-world gate reads selected native records; the descriptor carries a
607	display summary.** The guard covers **every `delete` and every `replace` edit** in
608	the plan — the unsafe-action set is those two actions, without qualification, and
609	this paragraph narrows it in no way. If the plan contains one, the prerequisite is
610	decided **before** any descriptor is built, and an `imported-prepared-declared`

613	
614	**A Run holds one `ClosedWorldV2` per Coverage entry, not one per Run, so the gate

623	It does not, and with several retained records that phrase did not denote. The

625

627	   and a universe in neither is **truly unrelated and does not veto**.

644	       contributes that universe.
645	     - A **selected but unavailable** binding (`universe=null`, whose `extents`
646	       remain "populated from host membership so expected file/package paths are
647	       not lost") contributes **typed unresolved ownership**: it holds a real
648	       retained expected-ownership claim with no universe to make eligible and no
649	       Coverage to establish a closed world, so it reports
650	       `REPAIR.CLOSED_WORLD_NOT_ESTABLISHED` and **does not vanish because some

652	     - An **unselected** binding is not a selected program and is never inferred.
653	     Each extent kind is read as itself: `file` and `package` are host membership
654	     extents, `symbol` is the selected program's **code** scope. All snapshot files
655	     are therefore **not** treated as every compiler's `programRootFiles`, and a

657	     unrelated**. Legitimate **multiple ownership is preserved** — one path
658	     analysed under two Rust targets or editions is two selected bindings with two

660	   * Retained **`source-path`** subject scopes (`file`, `clones`, `vcs-change`,
661	     all `universeRule: same-only`) are unioned in as an **additional retained
662	     witness**. They are **not** the owner census and cannot certify its
663	     completeness: their `subjectKindLaw` proves those scopes *name* paths, not
664	     that they *enumerate* every selected program owning one. A selected program
665	     with no such scope in this Run owns its extent just the same — which is
666	     exactly the case the census covers, and which is reachable: a universe bound
667	     only to a symbol-kind cell, owning a path through its retained symbol extent

669	     Ownership is never inferred from a path prefix, a display string, an optional

1466	## 3. Sealed dependency inputs (AR-07)
1467	
1468	### 3.1 `DependencySourceSetV1`
1469	
1470	Identity domain `native.dependency-source-set.v1`. Closed descriptor:
1471	`{schemaVersion:1, language:"rust", lockfileIdentity, packages:
1472	[DependencyPackageSourceV1…] sorted by (name, version, sourceId) UTF-8 bytes,
1473	completeness:{state, missing[]}}`.
1474	
1475	`DependencyPackageSourceV1`:
1476	
1477	| Field | Rule |
1478	|---|---|
1479	| `name`, `version` | exact `[[package]]` values from `Cargo.lock` |
1480	| `sourceKind` | `registry \| git \| path \| vendored` |
1481	| `sourceId` | exact `source` string from `Cargo.lock`, or `""` for path packages |
1482	| `lockChecksum` | 64-hex from the lock `checksum`, or `null` for git/path |
1483	| `fileManifestSha256` | H(`native.dependency-file-manifest.v1`, sorted `[{path, contentSha256, byteLength}]`) |
1484	| `fileCount`, `totalBytes` | exact uint64 |
1485	| `acquisition` | `{mode: in-snapshot-path \| in-snapshot-vendored \| imported-descriptor, descriptorId: ImportId\|null, vendorPath\|null}` |
1486	| `checksumVerification` | `tarball-matched \| self-consistent \| not-applicable \| mismatch` — `mismatch` refuses the whole set |
1487	| `provenanceAssurance` | `registry-authenticated \| declared` |
1488	
1489	Verification rules (feedback 3 corrected):
1490	
1491	- **DS-1 (registry, vendored tree)** A vendored directory carries a self-asserted
1492	  `.cargo-checksum.json`. Its `package` field equalling `lockChecksum` proves
1493	  nothing about the files: an attacker rewrites file contents and every `files`
1494	  entry while preserving `package`. The host therefore checks internal
1495	  consistency only (`package == lockChecksum`, every listed file's SHA-256
1496	  matches, no extra or missing files) and records `checksumVerification =
1497	  self-consistent`, `provenanceAssurance = declared`. Inconsistency is `mismatch`
1498	  and refuses the set. The reference model contains the mutation
1499	  (`ds1-mutation-preserving-package-checksum-stays-declared`): the mutated tree is
1500	  still admitted, and it is still *declared*, never authenticated.
1501	- **DS-2 (registry, tarball)** Only the exact `.crate` tarball whose SHA-256
1502	  equals `lockChecksum` yields `tarball-matched` / `registry-authenticated`. The
1503	  host extracts it deterministically into the CAS and computes the file manifest
1504	  itself. An extracted tree plus `.cargo-checksum.json` is DS-1.
1505	- **DS-3 (git)** The import supplies the checked-out tree for the exact `#rev`;
1506	  `not-applicable` / `declared`; the file manifest identity is the binding.
1507	- **DS-4 (path)** Path dependencies live in the snapshot; nothing is imported.
1508	- **DS-5 (no ambient reads)** `$CARGO_HOME/registry`, `~/.cargo`, `vendor/`
1509	  outside the snapshot, or any host path is read **only** as the explicit,
1510	  user-named source path of an import step (§7). Any acquisition mode outside the
1511	  closed set, or any fetch URL, refuses. No network fetch exists in any first-party
1512	  code path (design invariant, conformance-checked; not a confinement claim).
1513	- **DS-6 (completeness)** The set is complete for a target when every package
1514	  activated by `UnifiedFeaturesV1` is present with `checksumVerification ≠
1515	  mismatch`. An incomplete set is admitted with `completeness.incomplete` and
1516	  typed `input-closure-incomplete` Coverage for dependent crates; it never blocks
1517	  syntax analysis.
1518	
1519	`declared` provenance is disclosed wherever the package matters: in the Plan
1520	(through the set descriptor), in `AuthorizedExecutionV2.owners[].provenanceAssurance`,
1521	and in the pre-execution sentence (§5.2). Facts derived from declared sources are
1522	still Plan-bound Coverage inputs; the disclosure is what changes.
1523	
1524	### 3.2 Custody and transport
1525	
1526	The host stores admitted dependency sources in its content-addressed store keyed
1527	by `fileManifestSha256`; Plan-bound by `dependencySourceSetId`. Transport uses
1528	protocol-3 frames `DependencySourceManifest / DependencySourceChunk /
1529	DependencySourceSeal / DependencySourceAccepted` (§9.2) with the same byte-exact,
1530	digest-verified, reject-before-use discipline as the snapshot. The worker mounts
1531	the accepted files read-only at `.opensip/deps/v1/<name>-<version>/…` in its
1532	private scratch materialization. Nothing is fetched lazily.
1533	
1534	### 3.3 Cargo configuration: verified carrier, exact flags (feedback 5, 10)
1535	
1536	Primary source (`doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html`, read 2026-09-06):
1537	Cargo reads `.cargo/config.toml` (and legacy `.cargo/config`) from the current
1538	directory and **every ancestor**, plus `$CARGO_HOME/config.toml`, merging arrays;
1539	it also honors `CARGO_*` environment overrides and knobs that select executables
1540	(`build.rustc`, `build.rustc-wrapper`, `target.*.linker`, `target.*.runner`),
1541	credentials and network. Stock Cargo has no switch that disables ancestor

34	## 2. Vertex domain and endpoint admission
35	
36	A graph endpoint is the tuple `(universe, kind, nativeSubjectId, packageManifestPath or empty)`. No persisted evaluation-subject object is required.
37	
38	**Vertex domain** of a query is the union of:
39	
40	1. Subject-inventory rows selected by the admitted proof `evaluationInputRefs` (`domain=subject-inventory`), with universe taken from the EnumerationPlan program binding `(cellOrdinal, programOrdinal)`. Package vertices include `packageManifestPath` from the inventory row path.
41	2. Source and target endpoints of facts actually projected for this operation (so an external resolved target that is not first-party inventory remains a lawful vertex).
42	
43	**Fault precedence** for a requested endpoint. Admission is **schema-first**: §8 step 1 admits the whole request against `graph-query.schema.json#/$defs/GraphQueryRequestV1`, whose `GraphEndpoint` requires `packageManifestPath` exactly when `kind=package` and forbids it otherwise. Every shape that schema refuses is therefore a malformed request, decided before any Run, view, availability observation or vertex is consulted.
44	
45	1. Malformed or incomplete syntax → `QUERY.PARAMS_MALFORMED`: not an object, extra properties, universe not 64-hex, kind outside `{file,symbol,package}`, empty native id, `packageManifestPath` on a non-package, **or a `package` endpoint without a non-empty `packageManifestPath`**. A missing package coordinate is an incomplete request, not an ambiguous one; its remedy is to supply the coordinate, as for every other malformed field. No placeholder coordinate is substituted to re-admit the request, and no schema refusal is reclassified by which field failed.
46	2. A well-formed **complete** tuple that resolves to more than one distinct admitted vertex → `QUERY.ENDPOINT_AMBIGUOUS`. This is the only route to that detail. Because this section defines an endpoint, and so a vertex, by its complete tuple, a complete tuple names at most one vertex of an admitted domain: this step is not reachable through `execute_graph_query` and is kept only as a closed refusal. An implementation that nevertheless observes two distinct vertex records for one complete tuple must refuse with `QUERY.ENDPOINT_AMBIGUOUS` and must never choose one.
47	3. Well-formed complete tuple that matches zero vertices → `QUERY.ENDPOINT_UNKNOWN`. Same native id in other universes does not convert a fully specified unknown tuple into ambiguity.
48	4. Otherwise the endpoint is admitted. A known isolated inventory vertex with no incident projected facts is lawful (empty neighbors, or a zero-hop path when start equals target).

89	
90	Uniform closed request params. Extra properties refuse. LogicalPath `subject`/`target` and the non-graph bag are forbidden on graph ops (`QUERY.PARAMS_MALFORMED`).

94	| `graph.neighbors` | `relation`, `minResolution`, `direction`, `endpoint` | `factViewDigests` | one row per distinct admitted `fact2` (two provenances = two rows) | same `fact2` once | incidence at the admitted endpoint |

The first BFS reach of the target is the selected shortest hop-count path and the lex-least `fact2` sequence among those shortest paths; search stops there. 103	breadth-first frontier starting at the admitted start vertex. For each expanded
104	vertex, process eligible directed hops in ascending UTF-8 `fact2`-id order.

106	enqueue a newly reached endpoint with its parent depth plus one. Do not expand

120	Public bound constants (schema `Bounds`; unchanged):

122	| Constant | Value |
123	|---|---|
124	| maxPageSize | 1000 |
125	| defaultPageSize | 100 |
126	| maxItemsPerOperation | 100000 |

132	**Visited-node law.** `visitedNodes` is the number of distinct canonical endpoints **entered** during this logical operation. Fact-id scans are not visits. Check the cap **before** entering an unvisited endpoint; do not increment past the cap. Neighbors enter only the query endpoint. Path and reach enter start, then each newly reached endpoint. Zero-hop path with `maxVisitedNodes=1` is exactly-at-cap complete when no further vertex is owed. One-edge path with `maxVisitedNodes=1` does not enter the target (`visitedNodes=1`, `truncated-bound` if that hop is owed).
133

155	
156	`QueryRefusal.termination()` is a StepTermination. The public failure carrier is CommandEnvelope major 3, `kind=failure`, nonempty `errors` of registered DomainDetail, and **no** `run` field. A query does not mint a Run. Reading an old Run does not commit a new Run. `runId` appears on termination only for indeterminate completeness of an already admitted Run.
157	
158	Failure `requestId` is an already reserved host observation (`host.requestId`, `req1_` + 32 hex). It is never hashed from request bytes and this reference model does not implement CSPRNG. Missing or malformed host RequestId is a **reference-call precondition** (`ReferenceCallPrecondition`), distinct from public request refusal. Optional envelope `projectId` is included only when the request projectId is schema-admitted; malformed projectId is omitted.
159	
160	Identity **availability** (foundation `EvidenceStore` / availability record) is a trusted current host observation. Its `availability.state` values (`foundation/identity-schemas.v3.json#/$defs/availability`) route exactly as follows, every refusal being operational-failed / `HOST.IO_FAILURE` (`faultCause=host-io`) / exit 4 with the named registered detail: `purged` → `evidence.purged`; `expired` → `evidence.expired`; `corrupt` → `evidence.corrupt`; `unavailable` → `evidence.missing`. `unavailable` has no detail of its own and none is invented: required evidence that cannot be supplied is the identity owner's missing-evidence carrier (`EvidenceUnavailable` → `evidence.missing`, identity-and-evidence §5), the same detail as missing retained bytes below. `retained`, `partial` and an omitted observation neither refuse nor grant: `close_run` still decides, and retained bytes it finds missing or corrupt refuse under the rows below. The observation cannot grant retained authority: `close_run` remains the positive admission. Omitted availability is not a grant and not a purge. This is the explicit identity §5 availability selector for `graph.neighbors`, `graph.path` and `graph.reach`: operational-failed / exit 4 applies even when the trusted observation precedes full Run replay. It does not change the other seventeen operations. In particular, workflow-owned `finding.show` and its `query-evidence-purged` golden retain request-rejected / REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED / evidence.purged / exit 2. Select by the admitted operation and owning contract, never by a filename, exception prefix or caller-supplied fault origin.

Groups remain semantically identical when they do not carry parent locators.
214	- Negative knowledge is the admitted proof emitWhen root `p` for every selected subject, not an advisory `pass`/gating flag or arbitrary retained child deficiencies. Complete determinate roots and the exact emitted set prove absence for a non-emitted fingerprint, even if another subject has a known finding. Advisory all-false roots also prove absence. Boolean AND(false, required unknown) is determinate false. Optional unknown remains true-indeterminate. A live known hit remains usable when other roots are unknown.
215	- Execution-inputs is required on a public admitted Run. Missing capture is `EVALUATION.PROJECTION_INPUT_INCOMPLETE`.
216	- Host-only compatibility projection after existing TCB admission of the same `closure2`: `{closureId, componentManifestDigest, listing:{path,sha256,bytes}, trustOrigin, compatibleClosures, tree, platform, protocolMajor}`. `trustOrigin` is retained-generation / installed-signed-release / signed-closure-bundle. Select the unique reserved tree path; compare exact retained blob SHA-256 and length. Path absent is no declaration. Empty `compatibleClosures` is a complete listing. Present malformed / unrecognized / missing / hash-or-length mismatch refuses (never silent no-declaration). Request maps never assert trust or admission. Signature verification remains security TCB.
217	- ScopeDocument matching follows the normative [portable glob contract](../foundation/glob-pattern-contract.v1.md). The reference implements its include/exclude law with `W.in_scope` / `W.glob_match`; `**/*.ts` matches root `a.ts`, and terminal `src/**` includes `src/legacy.js`.
218	- A now-absent path inside a complete covering foundation scope may be determinate absence (deleted-file CODE-FIXED). A path outside the foundation walk is unexamined even if a wider ScopeDocument names it.

        val = resolve(doc, ptr)

1696	## 4. Resolution completeness (AR-12)
1697	
1698	### 4.1 Two different completeness claims
1699	
1700	A Coverage entry commits two things that were previously conflated:
1701	
1702	1. **Examined universe** — the exhaustive examined subject/target partition
1703	   (`subjectScopeCommitment`, retained). "Did we look at every subject?"
1704	2. **Resolution completeness** — whether every reference/import/call edge
1705	   originating in the examined subjects was resolved to a binding at the requested
1706	   rung, *after resolution was actually attempted over the whole partition*.
1707	   "Could we see every consumer?"
1708	
1709	### 4.1a Producing recipe for `subjectScopeCommitment` (closed)
1710	
1711	The retained C-2 selector deferred computation and verification. This is the successor
1712	recipe; nothing about the historical artifact changes.
1713	
1714	**Recipe.** `subjectScopeCommitment` is the foundation **subject-scope** identity of the
1715	examined partition, re-spelled in the native `Sha256Text` text form:
1716	
1717	```
1718	scope2      = identity-and-evidence H("subject-scope", D)          -> "scope2:"  + hex
1719	commitment  = "sha256:" + the same 64 hex                          -> Sha256Text
1720	```
1721	
1722	where `D` is the closed foundation record
1723	`identity-schemas.v3.json#/$defs/subject-scope`
1724	`{schemaVersion: 2, snapshotId, sourceUniverse, targetUniverse, relation, resolution,
1725	enumeratorClosure, subjects}`.
1726	
1727	**Inputs, exactly, and where each comes from.** `snapshotId` is the admitted `snapshot2`.
1728	`relation`/`resolution` are the Coverage key's own relation and rung. `sourceUniverse` and
1729	`targetUniverse` are the bare 64-hex universe digests of the same key (§2, §11).
1730	`enumeratorClosure` is the `closure2` of the Plan-bound enumerator that produced the
1731	partition. `subjects` is the **complete** examined subject inventory that enumerator
1732	enumerated over that snapshot, a canonical set (foundation ordering, duplicates refuse
1733	rather than dedupe). **Encoding**: the foundation canonical encoder and `H` frame, imported,
1734	not restated. There is **no native `H` domain for this field**: one preimage, one digest,
1735	two admitted textual spellings (§11).
1736	
1737	**Join with `scope2`.** The commitment is the *identical* digest to the `scope2` the host
1738	binds into the `coverage2` descriptor (`coverage.scopeId`). It is therefore not a second
1739	commitment and cannot drift from the scope it names. Its purpose is that the Coverage
1740	*payload* — the bytes whose `payloadDigest` mints `coverage2` — carries the provider's
1741	in-band commitment to the partition it claims to have examined, which the host then checks
1742	against a value the provider never supplied.
1743	
1744	**Where it is produced and checked (`admit_coverage_result_v3`, the admitted native producer
1745	boundary).** For every `CoverageResultV3` a provider sends, before any `coverage2` exists:
1746	
1747	1. The host builds `D` from **its own** enumeration and mints `scope2`. A provider-supplied
1748	   commitment is never an input to this step.
1749	2. `key.relation`, `key.resolution`, `key.sourceUniverse`, `key.targetUniverse` must equal
1750	   `D`'s (`native.coverage-key-scope-mismatch:<field>`).
1751	3. `key.subjectScopeCommitment` must equal the computed commitment
1752	   (`native.subject-scope-commitment-mismatch`).
1753	4. `entry.examinedUniverse.subjectScopeCommitment` must equal the key's
1754	   (`native.examined-universe-commitment-mismatch`) and
1755	   `entry.examinedUniverse.subjectCount` must equal `len(D.subjects)`
1756	   (`native.examined-universe-subject-count-mismatch`). A provider that examined a narrower
1757	   partition than the host enumerated is detected here, and by nothing else.
1758	5. RC-2 (§4.3) is rechecked over the same partition.
1759	6. Only then is `coverage2` minted from `{schemaVersion: 2, scopeId, payloadSchemaDigest,
1760	   payloadDigest}`. `payloadSchemaDigest` is the raw SHA-256 of the **exact registered schema
1761	   DOCUMENT bytes** (§7.2). A caller may restate it but never choose it: a value that is not the
1762	   registered document's digest refuses `native.coverage-payload-schema-not-registered`
1763	   (`coverage-payload-schema-digest-a-caller-chose-is-refused`).
1764

7	 "multiCauseAndPrecedence": "An entry carries ONE deficiency and simultaneously carries every carrier this registry names. Which single deficiency is declared when several apply is the section 10 precedence order, applied by the owning sufficiency evaluation against a REQUIREMENT. 2167	### 4.8 Type derivation provenance (feedback 12)
2168	
2169	The v1 draft capped JSDoc-free JavaScript type facts at `confidenceMillionths ≤
2170	900000`. That number had no evidence rationale: a compiler-inferred type is exact
2171	under the admitted universe, and JSDoc presence is not a calibrated probability.
2172	Replacement: every `types@checked` fact carries `TypeDerivationV1` =
2173	`{derivationKind: annotated|jsdoc-declared|compiler-inferred, confidenceMillionths:
2174	1000000, confidenceMethod: "native.confidence.v1", checkJs, limitations}`.
2175	`native.confidence.v1` is the versioned, conformance-bound method
2176	"declared-exact: every admitted checked fact is 1000000 under its universe; no
2177	value below 1000000 is produced by a native provider". Rule authors express
2178	"declared types only" through `derivationPolicy=declared-only` (§4.2), which
2179	yields the typed `derivation-policy-unmet` deficiency, not a fake percentage.
2180	`checkJs` is recorded because it changes diagnostics, not derivation.
2181	
2182	**The two clauses have different scopes, and the second is deliberately the wider
2183	one.** The first names the method of `TypeDerivationV1`, whose
2184	`confidenceMillionths` is a schema **constant** `1000000` and whose
2185	`confidenceMethod` is the constant `native.confidence.v1`: that record exists only

2186	on a `types@checked` fact. The second — *no value below 1000000 is produced by a
2187	native provider* — is **not** narrowed to `types@checked`. It is a **provider
2188	emission law** over this whole bundle: no native provider of any relation emits a
2189	confidence below 1000000, because a native fact is exact under its admitted
2190	universe and this design publishes no calibrated probability for any relation. It
2191	is not read as types-scoped, and reading it that way would be a *weakening* — it
2192	would permit a native `clones` or `references` provider to emit a fabricated
2193	percentage, which is exactly what §4.8 removed.
2194	
2195	That leaves `ViewEntryV3.confidenceMillionths`, whose domain is the full integer
2196	range 0…1000000 and which carries **no** `confidenceMethod`. The wider domain is
2197	deliberate and is what keeps §4.6 step 3 reachable: the floor comparison is the
2198	sufficiency evaluation's, it runs for **every** relation, and it must still decide
2199	correctly against an entry a conforming native provider would never have emitted —
2200	a defective or non-conforming provider, and the defensive fixture below. No
2201	*imported* route is offered as an example and none is implied: imported evidence
2202	is a separate plane that mints no `ViewEntryV3` at all (§7, workflows §4), so it
2203	could not supply one of these values, and inventing such a path to explain the

2209	to the emission law and is not evidence that any native provider emits such a

2279	
2280	1. **The values are per execution mode.** `native.prepare` runs owners as child
2281	   processes, so the `child-process` column is the applicable one. In v9's

2283	   `DISCLOSURE-ONLY`, because a component sharing the host's address space shares

2317	### 5.3 What the preparation step does (feedback 4)
2318	
2319	Owned by the host resolved-inputs adapter (never the semantic worker), after
2320	snapshot seal and dependency-source admission, before PlanId:
2321	
2322	1. Verify the carrier (§3.3 CC-1..CC-5); materialize snapshot and dependency
2323	   sources read-only in private scratch; write the single projected
2324	   `.cargo/config.toml`; construct the environment.
2325	2. Check current trust and revocation state (security owner's clock), then for
2326	   each owner in order: re-check revocation (`before-each-owner`), run the bundled
2327	   Cargo to compile and execute the build script or to build the proc-macro crate
2328	   for the selected cfg set (`cargo check --offline --frozen --locked --target
2329	   <triple>` restricted to the owners; the linker used is the closure linker;
2330	   nothing is installed).
2331	3. **Inside this same authorized step**, drive the bundled compiler's expansion
2332	   through the closure proc-macro server for every invocation site in the
2333	   workspace and dependency crates that names one of the built proc-macro crates,
2334	   and capture the expanded token text per site as `macro-expansion` rows; capture
2335	   `cargo:` directive output as `build-script-directives` rows. Loading the
2336	   proc-macro dylib *is* executing repository code; it happens here, under the
2337	   principal, with the live boundaries, and nowhere else.
2338	4. **Capture required generated data, discard executable products** (R2). For
2339	   each build-script owner: capture the `cargo:` directive lines as a
2340	   `build-script-directives` row; capture as `generated-file` rows the regular
2341	   data files under `OUT_DIR` named by the crate's
2342	   `include!/include_str!/include_bytes!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), …))` sites when
2343	   those are statically determinable, else every regular data file under
2344	   `OUT_DIR` within the PO-4 bounds; discard the build-script binary, every
2345	   dylib/object/archive/executable product and unreferenced scratch files; discard
2346	   the proc-macro dylibs. Referenced paths the script did not produce are recorded
2347	   (`missingReferencedPaths`) and become typed unknowns at analysis. Nothing of
2348	   `OUT_DIR` survives except the captured data rows
2349	   (`preparation-capture-keeps-referenced-data-discards-executable-products`).
2350	   The result is `PreparedOutputSetV3` (`kind: authorized-execution`).
2351	
2352	The semantic worker then consumes the inert set through the protocol
2353	(`PreparedOutputManifest/Chunk/Seal`), looks up expansions by exact site key, and
2354	executes nothing. `RepositoryResolutionV3.workerExecutesRepositoryCode` is the
2355	constant `false`. An external preparer may supply the same inert shape
2356	(`kind: imported-descriptor`, `declared` provenance, §3.6 PO-3); it can never
2357	supply a dylib.

2359	### 5.4 Failure, retry, cancellation, recovery
2360	
2361	| Event | Outcome |
2362	|---|---|
2363	| Owner build script exits non-zero | row `failed`; other owners continue; owner analyzed non-prepared |
2364	| Revocation observed before an owner | step stops; no further owner runs; rows already captured are discarded; `request-rejected` (`native.execution-not-authorized`) |
2365	| Wall or byte bound exceeded | whole step `operational-failed` (4); no row admitted. Existing `HOST.IO_FAILURE` with detail `native.prepare-bound-exceeded`. Not `BudgetExhausted`: a preparation bound is a safety bound of the adapter |
2366	| Cancellation | kill the process group, discard partial OUT_DIR and captured rows, `interrupted` (130) |
2367	| Retry | idempotent by `(dependencySourceSetId, toolchainDigest, cfgSetId, owners manifest)`; an identical inert set already in custody is reused without re-execution and without re-prompt when a policy record covers it |
2368	| Host crash mid-step | scratch reclaimed by ordinary crash reconciliation; no partial set is visible to Plan construction |
2369	| Ambient Cargo config found | `operational-failed` (4), `native.ambient-cargo-config`; never merged |
2370	| Imported set replaces in-host preparation | allowed; PO-0/PO-1/PO-3 apply |

2382	## 6. Clone equivalence modes (AR-13)
2383	
2384	### 6.1 Modes and evidence levels
2385	
2386	| Mode | Level/algorithm | Evidence level (closed) | Authority |
2387	|---|---|---|---|
2388	| `exact` | `L0-verbatim` | `byte-identical` | fact |
2389	| `normalized` | `L1-lexical` (default) or `L2-comment-insensitive` (opt-in) | `lexically-identical` / `comment-insensitive-identical` | fact |
2390	| `structural` | `L3-identifier-insensitive` | `identifier-insensitive-identical` | fact |
2391	| `near` | `near-v1`: Jaccard over 5-gram shingles of the L3 token stream | `similar-candidate` | candidate only |
2392	| `cross-tsjs` | `tsjs-erasure-v1` projection, then L3 | `cross-language-syntax-candidate` / `excluded` | candidate only |
2393	
2394	No semantic equivalence is inferred by any mode.
2395	
2396	### 6.2 Parameters (selected)
2397	
2398	`minOccurrences 2`; `minBodyBytes 64` (exact); `minTokens 20` (L1–L3,
2399	cross-tsjs); `minTokens 50` (near); `nearThreshold 800000` millionths;
2400	`maxCandidatesPerGroup 4096`; `maxGroupsPerUniverse 1000000`.
2401	
2402	### 6.3 Bodies and language-specific exclusions
2403	
2404	Body spans are function, method, closure/lambda, `impl` item and block bodies.
2405	**Import exclusion means candidate exclusion, not byte editing** (R5): a span that
2406	consists solely of import/`use`/`extern crate`/top-level `require` declarations,
2407	module/file headers, shebangs, license headers, `#![...]` inner attributes or
2408	`declare`-only TypeScript declarations is an *import-only body* and is excluded
2409	as a clone candidate in every mode. A body that is kept is hashed over its
2410	**exact verbatim bytes**: an internal `use`, `import()`, `require` or directive
2411	inside a function body is part of the preimage and is never stripped, rewritten
2412	or normalized away at L0 (`clone-import-only-body-excluded-and-kept-bodies-hash-verbatim`:
2413	two bodies differing only by an internal `use` line are not exact clones).
2414	
2415	| Language | Kept significant at every level | L2 removes | L3 renames |
2416	|---|---|---|---|
2417	| TypeScript/JavaScript | string/template literal contents, regex literals, JSX text, `'use strict'`/`'use client'` directives, `/// <reference>` and `// @ts-*` directives, decorators | non-directive comments | local `let/const/var`, parameters, local function names, destructured locals; **not** properties, imports, exports, globals, `this` members |
2418	| Rust | macro invocation token trees verbatim, attributes including `#[cfg]`, string/byte/raw literals, lifetimes | non-doc comments | local `let` bindings, parameters, closure parameters, pattern bindings; **not** fields, paths, generics, trait names, macro-introduced names |
2419	
2420	Fact identity is same-language: `languageId ∈ {typescript, javascript, rust}` is
2421	in the preimage, so a TypeScript body never groups with a JavaScript or Rust body
2422	in `exact`/`normalized`/`structural`, even with identical bytes.
2423	
2424	### 6.4 TS/JS cross-language decision (feedback 9)
2425	
2426	Decision: `languageId` **stays** in exact fact identities (a `.ts` and a `.js`
2427	body are different facts). Cross-TS/JS matching is a separate **candidate-only**
2428	mode `cross-tsjs` under the named deterministic syntax projection
2429	`tsjs-erasure-v1`:
2430	
2431	- Removed before L3 normalization: type annotations, `type`/`interface`
2432	  declarations, type parameter lists, `as` assertions, `satisfies`, non-null `!`,
2433	  definite-assignment `!`, `declare`/`readonly`/`abstract`/access modifiers,
2434	  `implements` clauses, `import type`/`export type`.
2435	- **Never removed**: tokens that TypeScript compiles into runtime behavior —
2436	  `enum`/`const enum`, parameter properties (`constructor(private x)`),
2437	  value-bearing `namespace`, decorators, `import =`. A body containing any of them
2438	  is **excluded** from cross matching with reason
2439	  `runtime-significant-ts-tokens` and the token list; it is not projected.
2440	- Output rows carry `projectionId=tsjs-erasure-v1`, `authority=candidate-only`,
2441	  `semanticEquivalenceClaimed=false`, `automaticDeletionEligible=false` as schema
2442	  constants. A cross candidate is never a baseline member, never a Control input,
2443	  never a repair prerequisite. Execution-inputs `CloneCandidateGroupV2.members`
2444	  are opaque candidate body IDs, not filesystem paths and not `subject3`
2445	  identity. Source custody lives on retained
2446	  `CandidateProducerResultV1.sourceBodies`; adapter maps are derived only from
2447	  that array. Each path must be in **this binding's** Plan
2448	  `candidateSourcePaths`. A caller locator map is not an authority input. Near
2449	  and cross-TS/JS remain candidate-only by this section; they mint no `fact2`
2450	  and no `relation@rung`.
2451	
2452	Cases: `clone-cross-tsjs-candidate-only`, `clone-cross-tsjs-runtime-significant-excluded`.

2454	### 6.5 Reviewed suppressions and false-positive boundary
2455	
2456	`CloneSuppressionV1` is a superseded draft transport shape, admitted by no product
2457	command. The single current review/suppression record is workflow ReviewDisposition.
2458	Its stable candidate key, mandatory finite expiry and advisory-only semantics are

2460	expired suppressions resurface. Fixed by

1	# Portable glob matching — version 1
2	
3	This normative owner specifies the matching predicate used by `GlobPattern`,
4	ScopeDocument path matching, and string field filters with `cmp: glob`. It makes
5	matching reconstructable without reference source code. The owning schema still
6	admits each pattern and candidate value; this predicate neither coerces values nor
7	changes those admission rules.
8	
9	## Matching law
10	
11	Matching is case sensitive and anchored to the entire candidate string. There is
12	no implicit prefix, suffix, recursive search, filesystem lookup, directory test,
13	or exclusion of dotfiles. Split both pattern and candidate at every literal `/`,
14	preserving empty segments. Do not resolve `.` or `..`, remove separators, rebase,
15	case-fold, or normalize Unicode in this predicate. A LogicalPath candidate must
16	already satisfy its owner; other admitted string fields need not be paths.
17	
18	An ordinary pattern segment matches exactly one candidate segment, in full:
19	
20	- `*` matches zero or more Unicode scalar values within that segment.
21	- `?` matches exactly one Unicode scalar value within that segment, not one byte
22	  or one displayed grapheme. Neither wildcard consumes `/`.
23	- Every other character matches itself. Braces and brackets have no expansion or
24	  character-class meaning. There is no escape syntax; the GlobPattern schema
25	  excludes backslash and NUL. Consecutive stars in an ordinary segment have the
26	  same matching power as one star.
27	
28	A pattern segment that is exactly `**` instead matches zero or more whole
29	candidate segments. This rule applies at the beginning, middle, and end, and may
30	consume the final filename segment. It does not require a directory. A segment
31	such as `a**b` is ordinary, and cannot consume a separator.
32	
33	Equivalently, let `P` and `S` be the split sequences. A match at `(i,j)` succeeds
34	at the end of `P` exactly when `j` is also at the end of `S`. For `P[i] = **`, it
35	succeeds if any `k` from `j` through `len(S)`, inclusive, makes `(i+1,k)` succeed.
36	Otherwise it succeeds exactly when `j < len(S)`, the ordinary segment matches
37	`S[j]`, and `(i+1,j+1)` succeeds. The predicate begins at `(0,0)`. This defines
38	results, not an implementation algorithm or a requirement to use recursion.
39	
40	## Required examples
41	
42	| Pattern | Candidate | Matches |
43	|---|---|---|
44	| `**/*.ts` | `a.ts` | true |
45	| `**/*.ts` | `src/nested/a.ts` | true |
46	| `*.ts` | `src/a.ts` | false |
47	| `src/**` | `src` | true |
48	| `src/**` | `src/legacy.js` | true |
49	| `src/**` | `src/nested/legacy.js` | true |
50	| `src/**/*` | `src` | false |
51	| `src/**/*` | `src/legacy.js` | true |
52	| `a/**/b` | `a/b` | true |
53	| `a/**/b` | `a/x/y/b` | true |
54	| `a/*/b` | `a/b` | false |
55	| `a**b` | `a/x/b` | false |
56	| `a**b` | `axxb` | true |
57	| `*` | `.hidden` | true |
58	| `a.ts` | `A.ts` | false |
59	| `a.ts` | `a.ts.extra` | false |
60	| `?.ts` | `é.ts` (one scalar before the dot) | true |
61	| `?.ts` | `é.ts` (`e` plus combining acute accent) | false |
62	| `[ab].ts` | `a.ts` | false |
63	| `[ab].ts` | `[ab].ts` | true |
64	| `{a,b}.ts` | `a.ts` | false |
65	| `{a,b}.ts` | `{a,b}.ts` | true |
66	
67	A trailing slash in a pattern is an empty final segment, not a directory flag.

2603	### 9.1 Versions and identity negotiation (feedback 1)
2604	
2605	`rust-semantic` protocol major **3**; `typescript-semantic` protocol major **2**.
2606	Capability tokens (closed, `CapabilityToken`): identity tokens
2607	`source-identity-snapshot2`, `plan-identity-plan2`, `fact-identity-fact2`,
2608	`coverage-v3`; plus `sealed-vfs-v1`, `multi-stage-analyze-v1`,
2609	`<lang>-semantic-facts-v1`, `resolution-completeness-v2`, `unresolved-edge-v1`,
2610	`dependency-source-v1` (Rust), `prepared-output-v3` (Rust), `native-context-v2`,
2611	and optional negotiated `target-attribution-v2`.
2612	`HelloV3` also carries `identityVersions: {snapshot:2, plan:2, fact:2, coverage:3}`
2613	and `HelloAckV3` must echo the token array and identity versions exactly.
2614	The four identity tokens remain `source-identity-snapshot2`,
2615	`plan-identity-plan2`, `fact-identity-fact2`, and `coverage-v3`.
2616	`target-attribution-v2` is an **additional optional capability**: it is not
2617	an identity token, is not required to spawn, and does not enlarge the
2618	identity token set. When present on both Hello and HelloAck, FactBatch
2619	payload is FactBatchV3. When absent, historical FactBatchV2 remains and
2620	occupancy is unknown except exact-id ephemeral. A FactBatchV3 payload
2621	without the token, or a FactBatchV2 payload with the token, is
2622	`PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION`.
2623	Protocol major stays 3 / TypeScript major 2. No new ProtocolLimitsV3 member;
2624	companions are bounded by existing `maxFactBatchCandidates` (4096) and
2625	`len(candidates)`.

2627	Reject-before-disclosure ordering:
2628	
2629	1. **Plan time (no spawn).** The host reads the signed capability row. The four
2630	   identity tokens are required for every worker; a row lacking any of them, or
2631	   any token the Plan needs, is never spawned: affected Coverage keys are
2632	   `unknown / provider-unavailable` (cause `capability-missing`). No raw
2633	   `snapshot2`, `plan2` or source byte reaches a worker that cannot name them
2634	   (`negotiation-v1-only-worker-never-spawned`).
2635	2. **Hello → HelloAck (no source bytes).** Exact recursive equality of the token
2636	   array and identity versions; mismatch → `FAULT`, `PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION`,
2637	   no snapshot, dependency or prepared byte is ever written.
2638	3. **OpenUniverse** carries `snapshot2`, `plan2`, the universe descriptor
2639	   including `nativeContext`, and `RepositoryResolutionV3`. The host state
2640	   machine admits it only when `identityNegotiated=true`; otherwise the run faults
2641	   with `sourceBytesSent=false` (`protocol3-open-universe-without-identity-faults`).
2642	4. Snapshot custody, dependency-source custody, prepared custody,
2643	   `NativeContextVerified`, then Analyze.
2644	
2645	Existing V1 relation payload grammars are reused unchanged inside `fact2` by
2646	exact `payloadSchemaDigest`; legacy FACT-ID-V1 identities remain historical and
2647	are never relabeled.

2729	Worker delivery is `OccupancyCompanionV1` on negotiated `FactBatchV3`. `FactCandidateV1` already carries opaque encoded

2735	`FactCandidateV1.canonicalRelationPayload` (JSON-vector

2743	Native §9.4 retains TS `delivery.v2` `AnalyzeV1.stageRequests`.

2853	## 10. Deficiencies, precedence and D9 mapping
2854	
2855	`DeficiencyV2` = fact-plane v1 values + `input-closure-incomplete`,
2856	`derivation-policy-unmet`, `resolution-incomplete`, `external-consumers-unknown`.
2857	Precedence (most specific first): `language-tier-unsupported`,
2858	`provider-unavailable`, `input-closure-incomplete`, `budget-exhausted`,
2859	`confidence-floor-unmet`, `derivation-policy-unmet`, `resolution-incomplete`,
2860	`external-consumers-unknown`, `required-relation-missing`.
2861	
2862	**Existing D9 codes only (R7).** No successor, interim or competing code exists in
2863	this contract; `d9_successor_codes()` is the empty list and `d9_map` refuses a row
2864	that names one. The native `deficiency` and `nativeCause` travel as **typed
2865	detail** inside the `coverage2` record (`CoverageResultV3.entry.deficiency` /
2866	`nativeCause`) that the host termination names by its `coverageId`; no D9 enum
2867	changes anywhere.
2868	
2869	**The Cause column is not one field.** This column previously read `Cause
2870	(nativeCause)` throughout, and three of its rows then named values the closed
2871	`NativeCause` enum cannot express: `computed-member-access`, `exports-open` and
2872	`compiler-inferred` each fail schema validation as a `nativeCause`. The only
2873	representable value for those rows was `null` — which that enum's own
2874	description defines as *a disclosure was owed and not made*, the exact argument
2875	that added the three `body-language-*` members. Worse, nothing compared the pair
2876	to anything, so a `resolution-incomplete` entry carrying the unrelated but
2877	schema-valid `lockfile-missing`, or relabelled `capability-missing`, or a
2878	`derivation-policy-unmet` over an empty `derivationKinds`, each closed a Run.
2879	
2880	The correction names the carrier per row rather than adding enum members, and
2881	that is a decision on the merits, not on compatibility: `resolution-incomplete`
2882	has a genuinely **set-valued** cause — an entry can exhibit up to all sixteen
2883	`UnresolvedEdgeKindV1` classes at once — so a scalar could only lose information
2884	or force an arbitrary pick, which is the multi-cause defect itself. All three
2885	rows already have closed, structured, independently derived carriers **in the
2886	same entry**: `resolutionCompleteness` (whose `unresolvedEdgeClasses` RC-2
2887	already forces to equal the admitted `unresolved-edge` facts of the view),
2888	`closedWorld.exportsClosed`, and `derivationKinds`. **No enum changes anywhere** —
2889	not `NativeCause`, not `DeficiencyV2`, not `UnresolvedEdgeKindV1`, not the public
2890	`DomainDetailCode` registry, and no D9 class, code or exit.
2891	
2892	Where the Carrier column says a field other than `nativeCause`, `nativeCause` is
2893	`null` **by design** and that null is no longer an escape: admission refuses
2894	unless the named field actually carries the cause. The pairing is closed in
2895	`native-evidence.schemas.v2.json#/x-opensip-deficiency-cause-registry`, derived
2896	at the producer boundary in `admit_coverage_result_v3` and therefore re-derived
2897	at retained Run closure, which re-runs that exact admission over the retained
2898	payload (`native.coverage-cause-*`, `PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION`).

2915	**Which surface the class and code columns govern.** They are the **whole-Run (or
2916	step) termination route** of a native deficiency and nothing else: the class, exit
2917	and reason code a host termination carries when that deficiency is the Run's
2918	primary deficiency. They are the D9 exit contract's own map, not a native choice —

2920	over its `D9Deficiency` vocabulary. Native owns only the bridge into that
